## pickle

Data Persistence

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html#module-pickle)

pickle_roundtrip_bounded: serialize a caller-supplied Python object to a pickle byte stream with an explicit protocol, then immediately deserialize it back using a restricted Unpickler whose find_class allowlist is supplied by the caller, returning the reconstructed object's type name and a digest of the stream without exposing arbitrary code execution.

**APIs**
- pickle.dumps(obj, protocol=..., fix_imports=..., buffer_callback=...)
- pickle.loads(data, fix_imports=..., encoding=..., errors=..., buffers=...)
- pickle.Pickler / pickle.Unpickler
- pickle.Unpickler.find_class(module, name)
- pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL
- pickle.DEFAULT_PROTOCOL
- pickle.PickleError / PicklingError / UnpicklingError

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"objRef":{"type":"string","description":"Opaque handle to an in-process object to serialize; the binding never accepts raw code."},"protocol":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":5,"description":"Pickle protocol; must be \u003C= HIGHEST_PROTOCOL."},"fixImports":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"allowedGlobals":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"module":{"type":"string"},"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["module","name"],"additionalProperties":false},"description":"Allowlist enforced by Unpickler.find_class during the roundtrip."},"maxBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Upper bound on serialized stream size."}},"required":["objRef","protocol","allowedGlobals","maxBytes"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"protocolUsed":{"type":"integer"},"byteLength":{"type":"integer"},"sha256":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[0-9a-f]{64}$"},"reconstructedType":{"type":"string"},"roundtripEqual":{"type":"boolean"},"error":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["ok","protocolUsed","byteLength","sha256","reconstructedType","roundtripEqual","error"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure in-memory computation: allocates a bytes buffer for the pickle stream and a reconstructed object graph; no filesystem, network or subprocess side effects. The restricted find_class prevents the documented arbitrary-code-execution vector of untrusted pickles. No installation, availability or execution on any worker is claimed.

**Constraints** Requires a CPython runtime exposing the pickle module (all supported CPython 3.x). Protocol 5 and PickleBuffer out-of-band transfer require Python 3.8+. Protocol 0/1/2 streams are Python-2-compatible only with fix_imports. Unpickling is inherently unsafe for untrusted data; this binding mandates an explicit allowlist and never unpickles data not produced by the same call. Not available on non-CPython implementations lacking pickle.

**Failure modes**
- PicklingError when objRef resolves to an unpicklable object (e.g. lambda, open file handle, local class)
- RecursionError on highly recursive object graphs
- UnpicklingError when find_class encounters a global not in allowedGlobals
- UnpicklingError on truncated or corrupted stream
- EOFError / AttributeError / ImportError / IndexError raised during unpickling
- ValueError when protocol exceeds HIGHEST_PROTOCOL or is negative beyond -1 semantics
- SizeLimitExceeded when serialized stream exceeds maxBytes
- BufferError when out-of-band buffers are required but not supplied

**Ranked use cases**
1. Safe roundtrip validation of in-memory objects before persisting them to a cache or database, catching unpicklable types early.
2. Enforcing a global allowlist policy for deserialization in a service that must consume pickled payloads from semi-trusted peers.
3. Measuring serialized size and digest of an object graph to decide between in-band and out-of-band (protocol 5) transfer.
4. Regression testing that a class's __getstate__/__setstate__ or __reduce__ implementation survives a pickle roundtrip across protocol versions.
5. Producing a canonical pickle stream fingerprint for content-addressed storage of Python object snapshots.

## pickletools

Python Language Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickletools.html#module-pickletools)

Disassemble a pickle byte stream into a bounded, structured opcode listing without executing pickle bytecode, using pickletools.genops to iterate (opcode, arg, pos) triples and pickletools.dis to render symbolic text into an in-memory buffer.

**APIs**
- pickletools.genops(pickle) — iterator yielding (opcode, arg, pos) triples; used to enumerate opcodes, decoded arguments and byte offsets for structured output.
- pickletools.dis(pickle, out=None, memo=None, indentlevel=4, annotate=0) — writes symbolic disassembly to a file-like object; used with an in-memory buffer to produce annotated text output.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"pickle_data":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded pickle bytes to disassemble (never executed)."},"annotate":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":0,"description":"Nonzero enables per-opcode short descriptions; value hints annotation column."},"indentlevel":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":4,"description":"Spaces of indentation per MARK level."},"max_opcodes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"default":10000,"description":"Upper bound on opcodes processed before truncation."},"include_text":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Whether to include the rendered dis() text."}},"required":["pickle_data"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"opcodes":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"code":{"type":"string"},"arg":{"type":["string","number","boolean","null"]},"pos":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["name","code","pos"],"additionalProperties":false}},"text":{"type":["string","null"]},"highest_protocol":{"type":["integer","null"]},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"opcode_count":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["opcodes","text","truncated","opcode_count"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only and side-effect free with respect to the pickle: no unpickling or execution of pickle bytecode occurs. Output is captured in memory; no files are written and no network or subprocess activity is performed.

**Constraints** Pure-Python standard library module; no native dependencies. Behavior and output formatting may vary across Python versions (e.g., color output added in 3.15). Must not be used as a substitute for safe unpickling of untrusted data. Bounded by max_opcodes and input size limits imposed by the host.

**Failure modes**
- Invalid base64 in pickle_data.
- Malformed or truncated pickle stream causing genops/dis to raise ValueError or similar.
- Unknown opcode encountered during iteration.
- max_opcodes exceeded, resulting in truncated=true rather than an error.
- Non-serializable decoded argument values (e.g., bytes) requiring string coercion.
- Memory pressure from very large pickles despite opcode cap.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Safely inspecting untrusted pickle files to understand structure without executing bytecode.
2. Debugging pickle serialization issues by mapping opcodes to byte offsets.
3. Building tooling to detect unused PUT/memo opcodes prior to applying pickletools.optimize.
4. Educational or audit tooling that explains pickle format opcodes to developers.
5. Regression testing that compares opcode sequences across Python versions or pickler configurations.

## pkgutil

Importing Modules

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pkgutil.html#module-pkgutil)

Enumerate submodules of a package path using pkgutil.iter_modules, returning a bounded, sorted list of ModuleInfo records (name, ispkg) without importing the submodules.

**APIs**
- pkgutil.iter_modules(path=None, prefix='') — yields pkgutil.ModuleInfo namedtuples (module_finder, name, ispkg) for submodules found on the given path list; used as the core enumeration primitive.
- pkgutil.ModuleInfo(module_finder, name, ispkg) — namedtuple describing a discovered module; its name and ispkg fields are projected into the output records.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"List of filesystem paths to scan; if omitted, top-level modules on sys.path are scanned."},"prefix":{"type":"string","default":"","description":"String prepended to every emitted module name."},"limit":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":10000,"default":1000,"description":"Maximum number of ModuleInfo records to return."}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"modules":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"ispkg":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["name","ispkg"],"additionalProperties":false}},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["modules","truncated","count"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only enumeration. Does not import the discovered submodules (only iterates finders), so no module-level side effects from submodules occur. May populate sys.path_importer_cache as a side effect of finder lookup. No filesystem writes.

**Constraints** Pure-Python standard library; no installation or availability on any worker is claimed. Only finders defining iter_modules() (e.g. importlib.machinery.FileFinder, zipimport.zipimporter) contribute results. Behavior depends on the runtime's sys.path and sys.path_hooks. Not a substitute for pkgutil.walk_packages (no recursion, no package imports).

**Failure modes**
- ValueError if path is provided but is not a list of strings.
- TypeError if prefix is not a string or limit is not an integer.
- OSError/UnicodeError when a sys.path entry cannot be used as a filename (mirrors os.path.isdir behavior).
- Finder without an iter_modules() method yields no results for that path item (silent omission, not an error).
- Truncation when discovered modules exceed limit; truncated flag set true.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Build a bounded inventory of importable submodules for a package directory to drive capability discovery tooling.
2. Detect whether a discovered name is a package vs. a plain module (ispkg) to decide whether further recursion is warranted.
3. Generate prefixed module name lists for plugin/extension registries without importing code.
4. Audit zip-importable modules by scanning zipimporter-backed paths.
5. Produce deterministic, sorted module listings for documentation or manifest generation.

## poplib

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/poplib.html#module-poplib)

poplib_mailbox_summary: connect to a POP3 or POP3-over-SSL server, authenticate, and return a bounded mailbox summary (message count, total octets, and per-message UIDL digests) without retrieving message bodies.

**APIs**
- poplib.POP3
- poplib.POP3_SSL
- POP3.user
- POP3.pass_
- POP3.stat
- POP3.uidl
- POP3.quit
- poplib.error_proto

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"port":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":65535},"use_ssl":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"timeout":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0},"username":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"password":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"max_messages":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":10000,"default":1000}},"required":["host","username","password"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"welcome":{"type":"string"},"message_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"mailbox_octets":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"messages":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"number":{"type":"integer","minimum":1},"uid":{"type":"string"}},"required":["number","uid"],"additionalProperties":false}},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["message_count","mailbox_octets","messages","truncated"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Opens an outbound TCP (or TLS) connection to the specified host and port; sends USER/PASS credentials in cleartext unless use_ssl or STLS is used; locks the mailbox on the server for the duration of the session; emits auditing events poplib.connect and poplib.putline; performs no local filesystem writes and does not retrieve or delete message bodies.

**Constraints** Not available on WASI/WebAssembly platforms. Requires network egress to the target host and port (110 plain, 995 SSL). timeout must be greater than zero. Credentials are transmitted in cleartext over plain POP3; TLS via POP3_SSL or STLS is recommended. POP3 is obsolescent; IMAP is preferred where supported. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- poplib.error_proto raised on protocol-level errors (bad greeting, authentication rejection, unsupported UIDL)
- socket-level errors (connection refused, DNS failure, timeout) propagate uncaught by poplib
- ValueError raised when timeout is zero (non-blocking socket creation prevented)
- ssl.SSLError / certificate verification failure when use_ssl is true and context validation fails
- Authentication failure leaves mailbox locked until quit(); caller must ensure quit() in finally block
- max_messages exceeded results in truncated=true rather than an error
- Server noncompliance with RFC 1939/2449 may yield malformed UIDL responses

**Ranked use cases**
1. Mailbox inventory and message-count monitoring for capability builders that need a lightweight, read-only POP3 probe
2. UIDL-based deduplication of already-processed messages before a separate retrieval step
3. Connectivity and credential validation for POP3 accounts in configuration or health-check tooling
4. Mailbox size and backlog reporting for quota or alerting workflows
5. Pre-fetch triage to decide which messages warrant full RETR/TOP retrieval in a downstream pipeline

## profile

Superseded modules

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/profile.html#module-profile)

profile.calibrate_bias: run profile.Profile.calibrate(ncalls) a bounded number of times with a caller-supplied timer and return the median per-event overhead bias as a float, without enabling profiling on any live code or writing profile data to disk.

**APIs**
- profile.Profile(timer=None, timeunit=0.0, subcalls=True, builtins=True)
- profile.Profile.calibrate(ncalls)
- profile.Profile.bias (class and instance attribute)
- time.perf_counter (as an example custom timer callable)

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"ncalls":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000000,"description":"Number of Python calls per calibration run passed to Profile.calibrate."},"repeats":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":25,"default":5,"description":"Number of calibration runs whose results are aggregated."},"timerName":{"type":"string","enum":["perf_counter","process_time"],"default":"perf_counter","description":"Named stdlib timer used as the Profile timer callable."},"timeunit":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"default":0.0,"description":"Multiplier for integer timer units."}},"required":["ncalls"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"bias":{"type":"number","description":"Median computed per-event overhead in seconds."},"samples":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"description":"Per-run calibration values returned by Profile.calibrate."},"ncalls":{"type":"integer"},"repeats":{"type":"integer"},"timerName":{"type":"string"},"consistent":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if sample spread is within a small relative tolerance."}},"required":["bias","samples","ncalls","repeats","timerName","consistent"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only with respect to user code: no profiling is enabled on live code, no stats files are written, and no global profile.Profile.bias is mutated. Only CPU time is consumed for the bounded calibration runs; the returned bias is reported to the caller and not applied anywhere.

**Constraints** Deprecated since Python 3.15 and scheduled for removal in 3.17; this is a design proposal only and is not claimed to be installed, available on any worker, or executed. Calibration accuracy is bounded by the underlying clock resolution (typically ~1 ms) and may yield negative per-event values at low call counts. Pure-Python implementation has significant overhead. Timer callables must return a single number or a list of numbers; os.times()-style tuples are accepted by profile but discouraged. Platform clock behavior differs across OSes.

**Failure modes**
- ncalls or repeats outside allowed bounds -> validation error before any calibration run
- timerName not in the allowed enum -> validation error
- calibrate returns non-numeric or negative values -> error reporting the offending sample
- samples inconsistent beyond tolerance -> result returned with consistent=false rather than raising
- interpreter terminated during calibration (e.g. sys.exit) -> no result produced
- module unavailable in the target interpreter -> import error surfaced, not masked

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders generating calibrated bias constants for deterministic profiling on a given platform before collecting stats.
2. Tooling that compares profile vs profiling.tracing overhead to justify migration decisions.
3. Test harnesses validating that a custom timer callable yields consistent calibration results.
4. Documentation and tutorial generators producing platform-specific calibration examples.
5. Regression checks that detect clock-resolution or timer regressions across Python builds.

## profiling

Debugging and profiling

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/profiling.html#module-profiling)

Run a bounded deterministic trace of a single Python callable using profiling.tracing and return pstats-compatible per-function statistics (direct time, cumulative time, call counts, primitive calls) for the top-N functions by cumulative time.

**APIs**
- profiling.tracing.run
- profiling.tracing (module)
- pstats.Stats

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"callableRef":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path to the zero-argument callable to trace, e.g. \u0027mypkg.mod.func\u0027."},"topN":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000,"default":20},"sortKey":{"type":"string","enum":["cumulative","tottime","ncalls"],"default":"cumulative"},"timeoutSeconds":{"type":"number","minimum":0.1,"maximum":600,"default":60}},"required":["callableRef"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"callableRef":{"type":"string"},"sortKey":{"type":"string"},"totalCalls":{"type":"integer"},"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"filename":{"type":"string"},"lineno":{"type":"integer"},"ncalls":{"type":"integer"},"primitiveCalls":{"type":"integer"},"tottime":{"type":"number"},"cumtime":{"type":"number"}},"required":["name","ncalls","primitiveCalls","tottime","cumtime"],"additionalProperties":false}},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["callableRef","sortKey","totalCalls","functions","truncated"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only with respect to the target program's data; executes the referenced callable in-process under the deterministic tracer, which instruments every call/return and adds moderate runtime overhead. No files are modified unless the implementation persists pstats output; no network access.

**Constraints** Requires Python 3.15+ where profiling.tracing exists; deterministic tracing is wall-clock only (no CPU/GIL modes, no attach-to-PID, no native/GC special frames). Not suitable for benchmarking (use timeit). Overhead is moderate and skews Python-vs-C comparisons. Single-process, single-threaded trace scope; bounded by timeoutSeconds and topN.

**Failure modes**
- ImportError/AttributeError when callableRef cannot be resolved to a zero-argument callable
- TypeError when the resolved object is not callable or requires arguments
- Timeout exceeded (timeoutSeconds) during traced execution; trace aborted and partial stats discarded
- Exception raised inside the traced callable propagates as a wrapped execution error
- Empty profile (no function calls recorded) yields empty functions array with totalCalls 0
- PermissionError when writing/reading temporary pstats data if implementation persists stats

**Ranked use cases**
1. Verify that a refactor reduced exact function call counts for a hot path
2. Capture complete call graphs including microsecond-scale functions missed by sampling
3. Produce pstats-compatible summaries for automated regression checks in CI
4. Identify caller/callee relationships for a specific entry point to guide optimization
5. Establish a deterministic baseline profile before applying statistical sampling in production

- profilePath is not a valid binary profile produced by this profiler
- Requested format is incompatible with stored profile data (e.g., opcode annotations absent from the binary)

## pty

Unix-specific services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pty.html#module-pty)

open_pty_pair: open a new pseudo-terminal master/slave file descriptor pair via pty.openpty() and return the descriptors with metadata, without spawning or attaching any process.

**APIs**
- pty.openpty() — opens a new pseudo-terminal pair and returns (master, slave) file descriptors; this is the core API the operation wraps.
- os.openpty() — underlying implementation pty.openpty() delegates to when available; role is the platform primitive for allocating the pty pair.
- os.close() — used to release descriptors on failure paths so the operation does not leak fds.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"close_on_failure":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If true, close any partially opened descriptors before raising."}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"master_fd":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"slave_fd":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"platform":{"type":"string"},"inheritable":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["master_fd","slave_fd","platform","inheritable"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Allocates two OS file descriptors (master and slave) in the calling process; no child process is created, no data is read or written, and no terminal state is modified beyond pty allocation. Descriptors remain open until the caller closes them.

**Constraints** Unix-only (Linux, FreeBSD, macOS primarily tested; other POSIX platforms untested). Not available on Windows. Descriptors are non-inheritable by default in Python 3.15+. Must not be mixed with higher-level system APIs on macOS per pty.fork() warning context. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- OSError/ENOSYS when the platform lacks pseudo-terminal support (non-Unix).
- OSError/EMFILE or ENFILE when the process or system file descriptor limit is exhausted.
- OSError/EACCES or EPERM when the process lacks permission to allocate a pty.
- Descriptor leak if close_on_failure is false and a later step fails; caller must close fds.
- Returned descriptors are process-local and invalid after fork/exec unless explicitly handled.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders needing a raw pty pair to drive interactive CLI programs programmatically (read/write master, feed slave as child stdio).
2. Terminal session recording/replay tooling analogous to script(1) that requires a controllable pseudo-terminal.
3. Test harnesses that emulate a controlling terminal for programs that insist on TTY detection.
4. Interactive automation of REPLs or password-prompting tools that refuse piped stdin.
5. Sandboxed command execution wrappers that need isolated terminal semantics per job.

**Effects** Writes or replaces a .pyc byte-code cache file at the resolved cfile path using importlib write-and-move semantics; may emit an error string to sys.stderr depending on doraise/quiet; does not modify the source file.

**Constraints** Requires a readable source file and a writable target directory; output path must not be a symlink or non-regular file; behavior depends on interpreter version (quiet added in 3.8, invalidation_mode in 3.7); SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH affects default invalidation mode; this is a design proposal only and does not imply installation, availability, or execution on any worker.

**Failure modes**
- PyCompileError raised when doraise is true and the source fails to compile (syntax error, encoding error, etc.)
- When doraise is false and quiet is 0 or 1, an error string is written to sys.stderr and pyc_path is null
- FileExistsError raised if the resolved cfile path is a symlink or non-regular file
- OSError/IOError when the source file is missing or unreadable, or the output directory is not writable
- Invalid optimize value or invalidation_mode not a member of PycInvalidationMode
- SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH environment variable influences the default invalidation_mode (CHECKED_HASH) when not explicitly set

**Ranked use cases**
1. Pre-compiling installed modules for shared use where end users lack write permission to the source directory's __pycache__
2. Build-system integration that generates .pyc files with UNCHECKED_HASH for reproducible, externally managed byte-code caches
3. CI validation step that compiles each source file and reports syntax/encoding errors as structured results
4. Packaging pipelines that precompile wheels or deployment artifacts to reduce first-import latency
5. Diagnostic tooling that surfaces PyCompileError details (file, line, message) for developer feedback

## pyclbr

Python Language Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pyclbr.html#module-pyclbr)

browse_module_source: given a Python module name and optional search path, statically extract a bounded, serializable outline of module-level and nested functions/classes (names, kinds, line numbers, async flag, parent path, and class base names) using pyclbr.readmodule_ex, without importing the target module.

**APIs**
- pyclbr.readmodule_ex(module, path=None) — primary API; returns a dict mapping top-level function/class names to Function/Class descriptors, with nested definitions under each descriptor's children attribute and package search path under '__path__'.
- pyclbr.Function — descriptor class whose attributes (file, module, name, lineno, parent, children, is_async) are read to build the outline.
- pyclbr.Class — descriptor class whose attributes (file, module, name, lineno, parent, children, super, methods) are read to build the outline and base-class names.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"module":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted module name to read, e.g. \u0027pkg.sub\u0027."},"path":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional sequence of directory paths prepended to sys.path for locating source."},"max_depth":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Maximum nesting depth of children to include; 0 means top-level only."},"include_bases":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether to include class base names in output."}},"required":["module"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"module":{"type":"string"},"is_package":{"type":"boolean"},"package_path":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"definitions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["function","class"]},"lineno":{"type":"integer"},"file":{"type":"string"},"is_async":{"type":"boolean"},"parent_path":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"bases":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"children":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}},"required":["name","kind","lineno","file","parent_path","children"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"required":["module","is_package","package_path","definitions"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only: reads source files from disk to parse them; does not import or execute the target module, so it is safe for untrusted code. No writes, no network, no global state mutation beyond temporary sys.path handling internal to pyclbr.

**Constraints** Only works on Python-coded modules; cannot describe standard or optional extension modules. Requires filesystem read access to module source. Behavior depends on sys.path and the supplied path. Descriptors are pyclbr objects and must be serialized to plain JSON-compatible structures. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError-like lookup failure when the named module's source cannot be located on the given path or sys.path.
- SyntaxError or other parse errors when the target source is not valid Python.
- Empty or partial results for modules not implemented in Python (extension modules), since pyclbr only reads Python source.
- Unresolvable base classes are reported as plain strings rather than Class descriptors; consumers must handle mixed types.
- Invalid input types (non-string module, non-sequence path) raise TypeError.
- Depth truncation may omit nested definitions when max_depth is too small.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Static code-outline extraction for documentation and API-index generation of Python packages.
2. Safe structural inspection of untrusted Python source without importing or executing it.
3. Building module-browser or IDE-style symbol trees with nesting and line numbers.
4. Dependency and inheritance mapping by collecting class base names for architecture analysis.
5. Detecting async function definitions and nested definitions for linting or migration tooling.

**APIs**
- pydoc.render_doc
- pydoc.Helper
- inspect.getcomments

```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"target":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted name of module, package, class, function, or method to document"},"max_chars":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000000,"description":"Upper bound on returned text length"},"include_private":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether to include underscore-prefixed members"}},"required":["target"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

## queue

Concurrent Execution

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/queue.html#module-queue)

bounded_put_with_timeout: attempt a single non-blocking-or-timeout-bounded insertion of one item into a caller-supplied queue.Queue instance, returning whether the item was accepted and the queue's approximate size afterward, without ever blocking indefinitely.

**APIs**
- queue.Queue.put(item, block=True, timeout=None)
- queue.Queue.qsize()
- queue.Full
- queue.ShutDown

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"item":{"description":"Opaque item to enqueue; must be JSON-serializable for transport but is passed through unchanged to the queue."},"block":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"timeout":{"type":["number","null"],"minimum":0,"default":null,"description":"Seconds to wait at most; null means no timeout (caller must accept potential blocking)."}},"required":["item"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"accepted":{"type":"boolean"},"qsize":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"reason":{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["full","shutdown",null]}},"required":["accepted","qsize","reason"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Mutates the caller-supplied queue by inserting at most one item; increments the unfinished-task counter used by join()/task_done(). No filesystem, network or process-level side effects. No installation or execution is performed or claimed.

**Constraints** Requires a live queue.Queue (or subclass) instance supplied by the caller; not usable across processes (multiprocessing.Queue is out of scope). Queue classes are not reentrant within a thread. On Windows and pre-3.0 POSIX, block=True with timeout=None performs an uninterruptible wait, so callers should prefer an explicit timeout. ShutDown semantics require Python 3.13+. SimpleQueue lacks task tracking and is excluded from this operation.

**Failure modes**
- queue.Full raised when block is false or timeout elapses with no free slot; mapped to accepted=false, reason="full".
- queue.ShutDown raised when the target queue has been shut down; mapped to accepted=false, reason="shutdown".
- TypeError/ValueError from invalid timeout (negative or non-numeric) rejected before calling put().
- Non-serializable item rejected at the transport boundary before reaching the queue.
- qsize() is approximate; reported size may not reflect concurrent producers/consumers.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Bounded producer hand-off: enqueue work items into a fixed-size FIFO with a timeout so a producer thread degrades gracefully instead of blocking forever when consumers stall.
2. Backpressure signaling in a pipeline: detect queue.Full to throttle or shed load and report qsize for observability.
3. Graceful shutdown coordination: detect queue.ShutDown to stop producers cleanly after shutdown(immediate=False) drains remaining tasks.
4. Priority scheduling: apply the same bounded-put contract to a PriorityQueue carrying (priority, data) tuples for ordered task dispatch.
5. Test harness for concurrency code: deterministically exercise Full/ShutDown paths by controlling maxsize and shutdown state.

## quopri

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/quopri.html#module-quopri)

Encode a bounded bytes payload to MIME quoted-printable text using quopri.encodestring, returning the encoded bytes as a string plus metadata; no file I/O, no decoding, no header Q-encoding beyond the documented underscore flag.

**APIs**
- quopri.encodestring(s, quotetabs=False, header=False) — performs the actual quoted-printable encoding of a bytes object and returns encoded bytes; this is the sole real API invoked by the operation.
- quopri.decode / quopri.decodestring — documented counterparts referenced only for round-trip validation in tests, not invoked by the operation.

**Input contract**

```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded bytes to encode; decoded to bytes before calling quopri.encodestring."},"quotetabs":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"Passed as quotetabs to quopri.encodestring; when true, embedded spaces and tabs are encoded."},"header":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"Passed as header to quopri.encodestring; when true, spaces are encoded as underscores per RFC 1522."},"maxInputBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1048576,"default":65536,"description":"Caller-declared bound; operation must reject payloads exceeding this."}},"required":["data"],"additionalProperties":false}
```


**Effects** Pure in-memory transformation; no filesystem, network, subprocess or environment mutation. No installation, availability or execution on any worker is claimed or implied.

**Constraints** Requires a Python 3 runtime exposing the documented quopri module; operates only on bytes, not str; bounded to maxInputBytes (<=1 MiB) to keep the operation bounded; no streaming file-object API (encode/decode) is exposed; behavior follows RFC 1521/1522 as documented; platform-independent aside from Python availability.

- InputTooLarge: decoded payload exceeds maxInputBytes.
- TypeError from quopri.encodestring if a non-bytes object is passed (should be prevented by validation).
- MemoryError on very large payloads within the declared bound.
- SchemaViolation: unknown fields or missing required 'data'.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders producing RFC 1521-compliant quoted-printable bodies for MIME email composition pipelines.
2. Round-trip test harnesses validating encode/decode symmetry against quopri.decodestring.
3. Pre-flight size/expansion estimation for text payloads before transport encoding.

## random

Numeric and Mathematical Modules

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/random.html#module-random)

seeded_sample: create an isolated random.Random instance from a caller-supplied seed and draw a bounded, reproducible sample without replacement from a caller-supplied population, returning the selected items and the generator state for later continuation.

**APIs**
- random.Random(seed) — constructs an independent generator instance so state is not shared with the global generator
- random.Random.sample(population, k) — performs sampling without replacement and returns a new list in selection order
- random.Random.getstate() — captures the generator's internal state so a later call can resume the same reproducible sequence

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"seed":{"type":["integer","string","null"],"description":"Seed for the isolated Random instance; null means system-derived seeding"},"population":{"type":"array","items":{},"minItems":1,"description":"Sequence of candidate items; may contain duplicates"},"k":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Number of unique positions to sample without replacement"}},"required":["seed","population","k"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"sample":{"type":"array","items":{},"description":"Selected items in selection order"},"state":{"type":"object","description":"Opaque serialized generator state from getstate() for resumption","additionalProperties":true},"seedUsed":{"type":["integer","string","null"]}},"required":["sample","state","seedUsed"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure computation in memory; no filesystem, network or global generator mutation. The global random module state is untouched because a dedicated Random instance is used. Output is deterministic for a given seed and Python version.

**Constraints** Not suitable for cryptographic or security purposes; use secrets instead. Reproducibility is only guaranteed for the same seed and compatible seeder across versions, and not under concurrent multi-threaded use of the same instance. SystemRandom is not used, so results are software-deterministic. Availability of the random module on the target platform is not asserted here.

**Failure modes**
- ValueError when k exceeds the population length (sample size larger than population)
- TypeError when population is not a sequence (e.g., a set) or seed is an unsupported type
- IndexError when population is empty
- Serialization failure if the captured state cannot be encoded for transport
- Non-reproducibility across Python versions if the compatible seeder guarantee is not relied upon

**Ranked use cases**
1. Reproducible train/test or holdout splits for data pipelines, seeded per run
2. Deterministic A/B or feature-flag assignment of items to cohorts
3. Raffle or lottery-style winner selection with auditable seed and resumable state
4. Monte Carlo and bootstrap resampling harnesses needing isolated, repeatable generators
5. Randomized test-data or fixture generation with replayable seeds

Text Processing Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html#module-re)

Compile a regular expression pattern once and return a bounded, serializable summary of its structure (group count, named groups, and a boolean validity flag) without performing any matching against input text.

**APIs**
- re.compile
- re.Pattern.groups
- re.Pattern.groupindex
- re.PatternError

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"pattern":{"type":"string","description":"Regular expression source text"},"flags":{"type":"integer","description":"Bitwise OR of re flag constants (e.g. re.I|re.M); defaults to 0"},"isBytes":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, treat pattern as an 8-bit bytes pattern; defaults to false"}},"required":["pattern"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"valid":{"type":"boolean"},"groupCount":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"namedGroups":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"integer"}},"errorMessage":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["valid","groupCount","namedGroups","errorMessage"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure computation: compiles the pattern in-process and reads metadata attributes. No filesystem, network, or global state mutation beyond the interpreter's internal regex compile cache. No matching, substitution, or text scanning is performed.

**Constraints** Requires a CPython 3.x runtime with the re module present; no installation or availability on any worker is claimed. str and bytes patterns cannot be mixed. re.LOCALE is only valid for bytes patterns. Group names in bytes patterns are restricted to ASCII. Output is a bounded metadata summary only; no Match objects are serialized.

1. Pre-validating user-supplied regex patterns before storing them in a configuration or rule registry
2. Enumerating named capture groups to auto-generate documentation or field mappings for a parsing pipeline
3. Detecting duplicate or conflicting group names across a set of patterns during schema design
4. Building a capability that classifies patterns by complexity (group count) to gate expensive downstream matching
5. Sanity-checking pattern/flag combinations (e.g. LOCALE vs ASCII) before deploying text-processing jobs

- rlcompleter.Completer.complete(text, state)


**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"mod_name":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute module name, e.g. \u0027pkg.mod\u0027 or \u0027pkg\u0027."},"run_name":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional __name__ override; null means default."},"init_globals":{"type":["object","null"],"description":"Optional JSON object of pre-populated globals; must be JSON-serializable and is not modified."},"include_globals":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional allowlist of global names to report; empty means report only the special names."}},"required":["mod_name"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**

**Effects** Executes arbitrary module code in the current process; may mutate sys.modules, sys.path, sys.argv and other interpreter state, and leaves cached imports and module-level side effects in place after return. The binding uses alter_sys=False to avoid the optional sys.argv/sys.modules manipulation, but runpy is explicitly not a sandbox and is not thread-safe when sys is touched.

**Constraints** CPython standard library only; requires the module to be locatable on sys.path. Not a sandbox: no isolation of side effects. Not thread-safe for sys manipulation; callers in threaded code should serialize or delegate to a separate process. __cached__ is no longer set as of 3.15; __loader__/__package__ setting deprecated since 3.12. Functions/classes defined by executed code are not guaranteed to work after return; importlib is preferred when that matters. This is a design proposal only — no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

- ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError when mod_name does not resolve via the standard import mechanism.
- ValueError or TypeError for a non-absolute or malformed mod_name.
- Any exception raised by the executed module code propagates; the binding reports it as a structured error and does not swallow it.
- Non-JSON-serializable init_globals rejected before execution.
- Package without a __main__ submodule fails when executed as a package.
- Partial side effects (cached imports, module-level state) persist in the process even on failure, since runpy is not a sandbox.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders implementing a safe '-m'-style module launcher that reports resolved spec, file and globals summary.
2. Pre-flight validation of plugin/entry-point modules before wiring them into a pipeline.

- scheduler.enter(delay, priority, action, argument=(), kwargs={})

**Input contract**

**Output contract**
```json

```

**Effects** In-memory only: constructs a scheduler, enqueues events, and executes due actions via run(blocking=False). No files, network, subprocesses or persistent state are touched; delayfunc may sleep up to the time budget. Actions are caller-supplied callables and their side effects are outside this binding's control.

Uses time.monotonic or time.time as timefunc; wall-clock accuracy depends on the platform. run(blocking=False) returns the delay to the next event or None when empty. Thread-safety of the scheduler class does not make caller actions thread-safe. No installation, availability or execution is claimed.

- Exception raised by an action propagates and that event is not retried on later run() calls

- time_budget exceeded before all due events run, leaving events in remaining

1. Deterministic simulation of delayed task ordering by priority for testing schedulers
2. Bounded retry/backoff orchestration for transient operations within a time budget

5. Teaching and validating event-ordering semantics (enter vs enterabs, priority ties)

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"fds":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"minItems":1},"eventmask":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":7},"timeoutSeconds":{"type":["number","null"],"minimum":0,"default":0}},"required":["fds","timeoutSeconds"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"ready":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"fd":{"type":"integer"},"events":{"type":"integer"},"readable":{"type":"boolean"},"writable":{"type":"boolean"},"error":{"type":"boolean"},"hangup":{"type":"boolean"},"invalid":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["fd","events","readable","writable","error","hangup","invalid"],"additionalProperties":false}},"timedOut":{"type":"boolean"},"elapsedSeconds":{"type":"number"}},"required":["ready","timedOut","elapsedSeconds"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

## signal

Networking and Interprocess Communication

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/signal.html#module-signal)

describe_signal: given a signal number, return a bounded, read-only description of that signal using signal.strsignal() and signal.Signals, without installing handlers, sending signals, or altering masks.

**APIs**
- signal.strsignal(signalnum) — returns the human-readable description of a signal number (e.g. 'Interrupt' for SIGINT) or None if no description exists; raises ValueError for invalid numbers.
- signal.Signals — IntEnum collection of SIG* constants used to map a numeric signal to its symbolic name and to validate membership.
- signal.valid_signals() — returns the set of valid signal numbers on the platform, used to bound and validate the requested number.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"signalnum":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["signalnum"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"signalnum":{"type":"integer"},"name":{"type":["string","null"]},"description":{"type":["string","null"]},"valid":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["signalnum","name","description","valid"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only and side-effect free: no signal handlers are installed, no signals are sent, no signal masks are modified, and no timers are set. Only queries strsignal, Signals and valid_signals.

**Constraints** Must run in the main thread of the main interpreter for any handler-related operations, though this operation itself only reads. Signal availability is platform-specific: many SIG* names are Unix-only, Windows supports only a subset (SIGABRT, SIGFPE, SIGILL, SIGINT, SIGSEGV, SIGTERM, SIGBREAK), and on WebAssembly signals are emulated with several functions/signals unavailable. SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be caught, blocked or ignored. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- ValueError if signalnum is not a valid signal number on the platform (propagated from strsignal).
- TypeError if signalnum is not an integer.
- signalnum not present in signal.Signals enum: name returned as null while description may still be available.
- Platform-dependent absence of a given SIG* constant (AttributeError if code references a name not defined on the system).

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders validating and labeling signal numbers before wiring any handler logic, using strsignal and Signals for human-readable names.
2. Diagnostic tooling that maps raw signal numbers from logs or crash reports to symbolic names and descriptions.
3. Cross-platform capability gating: checking valid_signals() to decide which signal-based features a builder may expose on a given platform.
4. Documentation/help generation that enumerates Signals members with their strsignal descriptions.
5. Input sanitization for higher-level signal-handling capabilities, rejecting invalid signal numbers early with clear errors.

## site

Python Runtime Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#module-site)

Inspect a single site-packages directory's startup configuration without applying it: parse the directory's .pth and .start files and report the path extensions, deprecated import lines, and .start entry points that would be recorded, using site.StartupState.addsitedir() to accumulate state and reading the recorded data without calling process().

**APIs**
- site.StartupState
- site.StartupState.addsitedir
- site.makepath
- site.getsitepackages
- site.getusersitepackages
- site.ENABLE_USER_SITE

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"sitedir":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute path of the site-packages directory to inspect."},"known_paths":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional case-normalized paths used to suppress duplicate sys.path entries; defaults to current sys.path when omitted."}},"required":["sitedir"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"sitedir":{"type":"string"},"exists":{"type":"boolean"},"pathExtensions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"deprecatedImportLines":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"startEntryPoints":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"pthFiles":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"startFiles":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"errors":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["sitedir","exists","pathExtensions","deprecatedImportLines","startEntryPoints","pthFiles","startFiles","errors"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only inspection: constructs a site.StartupState, calls addsitedir() to record data, and reports it without calling process(). No sys.path mutation, no entry point invocation, no import-line execution, and no builtins modification occur. The caller's interpreter state is unchanged.

**Constraints** Requires Python 3.15+ for site.StartupState and .start file support; on earlier versions only .pth parsing is available and .start reporting must be omitted. Behavior depends on platform path layout (Windows vs Unix/macOS, free-threaded 't' suffix). Does not honor -S semantics beyond what the caller passes. Must not call process() on the state, since it is non-idempotent. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- sitedir is not an absolute path or is not a string
- sitedir does not exist or is not a directory (reported via exists=false, not raised)
- PermissionError reading a .pth or .start file
- UnicodeDecodeError on a .start file not encoded in UTF-8
- Malformed .start entry point lacking the mandatory pkg.mod:callable form (recorded in errors, processing continues)
- Invalid known_paths entries that are not case-normalized strings
- OSError from os.path.abspath() inside makepath() (falls back to joined path per documented behavior)

**Ranked use cases**
1. Audit a site-packages directory for deprecated import lines in .pth files ahead of the 3.18/3.20 removal, to plan migration to .start entry points
2. Inventory .start entry points that will run at interpreter startup, for supply-chain and startup-cost review
3. Verify that path extensions in .pth files resolve to existing directories before relying on them
4. Diagnose why a package's startup hook is not running by comparing .pth import lines against a same-named .start file
5. Build a capability-builder report of site configuration across global and user site-packages directories without mutating sys.path

## sitecustomize

Python Runtime Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#module-sitecustomize)

Inspect sitecustomize startup customization state for a given interpreter prefix without importing or executing sitecustomize: resolve the candidate sitecustomize module location on sys.path and report whether it is importable, using site.getsitepackages() and importlib.util.find_spec() to locate it without executing it.

**APIs**
- site.getsitepackages
- importlib.util.find_spec

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"prefixes":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional list of prefix directories to compute site-packages paths from; defaults to site.PREFIXES when omitted."},"module_name":{"type":"string","enum":["sitecustomize"],"default":"sitecustomize"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"module_name":{"type":"string"},"site_packages":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"found":{"type":"boolean"},"origin":{"type":["string","null"]},"search_locations":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["string","null"]}}},"required":["module_name","site_packages","found","origin","search_locations"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only. Does not import or execute sitecustomize, does not modify sys.path, does not run .pth or .start files, and does not alter builtins. No filesystem writes.

**Constraints** Only meaningful when site processing is enabled; under -S the site module is not auto-imported and sitecustomize is never attempted, so results describe potential rather than actual startup behavior. Does not reflect virtual-environment include-system-site-packages resolution beyond what site.getsitepackages reports. Must not be used to trigger or simulate startup customization.

**Failure modes**
- find_spec raises ModuleNotFoundError or ValueError for malformed module_name (only 'sitecustomize' accepted)
- find_spec may raise ImportError if a parent package in the search path is broken
- site.getsitepackages may return paths that do not exist; existence is not verified
- Permission or OSError while stat-ing candidate paths surfaces as an exception
- Non-Unix platforms where sys.prefix/sys.exec_prefix are empty yield empty site_packages list

**Ranked use cases**
1. Audit whether a sitecustomize module is present and where it would be resolved from on a given interpreter prefix, without executing it.
2. Diagnose silent startup failures by confirming sitecustomize resolution before investigating arbitrary exceptions raised during its import.
3. Inventory site-packages directories and candidate customization modules across multiple prefixes for environment documentation.
4. Verify that a deployment placed sitecustomize in an expected site-packages location rather than a shadowing path earlier on sys.path.
5. Support migration planning from .pth import lines to .start entry points by confirming which customization module is discoverable at startup.

## smtplib

Internet Protocols and Support

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/smtplib.html#module-smtplib)

send_plaintext_email: open a bounded SMTP session (optionally STARTTLS), authenticate if credentials are supplied, deliver one ASCII message to a bounded recipient list, and always close the session.

**APIs**
- smtplib.SMTP
- smtplib.SMTP.sendmail
- smtplib.SMTP.starttls
- smtplib.SMTP.login
- smtplib.SMTP.quit
- smtplib.SMTPRecipientsRefused
- smtplib.SMTPSenderRefused
- smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError
- smtplib.SMTPNotSupportedError
- smtplib.SMTPServerDisconnected

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"port":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":65535},"use_starttls":{"type":"boolean"},"username":{"type":"string"},"password":{"type":"string"},"from_addr":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"to_addrs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":1,"maxItems":100},"subject":{"type":"string"},"body":{"type":"string"},"timeout_seconds":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0,"maximum":120}},"required":["host","from_addr","to_addrs","subject","body"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"delivered":{"type":"boolean"},"refused_recipients":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["integer","string"]}}},"server_response_code":{"type":"integer"},"tls_used":{"type":"boolean"},"authenticated":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["delivered","refused_recipients","tls_used","authenticated"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Opens an outbound TCP connection (and TLS session when requested), transmits envelope and message bytes to the remote SMTP server, emits the smtplib.SMTP.send auditing event, and closes the connection via quit() on all paths. No local filesystem writes.

**Constraints** Not available on WASI/WebAssembly. Requires outbound network access to the SMTP host and port; sandboxed workers without egress will fail at connect. Message body is restricted to ASCII in this proposal; SMTPUTF8 is out of scope. timeout_seconds must be greater than zero (zero raises ValueError per the module). Credentials are passed as plain input fields and must be handled as secrets by the caller. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- SMTPConnectError or TimeoutError when the connection cannot be established within timeout_seconds
- SMTPServerDisconnected if the server drops the session mid-transaction
- SMTPHeloError if the server rejects EHLO/HELO
- SMTPNotSupportedError if use_starttls is true but STARTTLS is not advertised
- SMTPAuthenticationError if credentials are rejected
- SMTPSenderRefused if from_addr is refused
- SMTPRecipientsRefused if every recipient is refused
- SMTPDataError if message data is rejected
- ValueError if timeout_seconds is zero or the message contains non-ASCII characters without SMTPUTF8 handling

**Ranked use cases**
1. Deliver a single operational notification (job completion, alert) from a capability builder to a fixed recipient list over an authenticated SMTP relay
2. Send a generated report or summary as a plaintext email body to a bounded set of internal recipients
3. Provide a minimal outbound mail primitive for workflow automation that must notify humans on failure conditions
4. Exercise SMTP connectivity and authentication as a health-check step in a deployment pipeline
5. Relay a short ASCII message from an agent to a localhost or internal SMTP listener for integration testing

## socketserver

Internet Protocols and Support

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/socketserver.html#module-socketserver)

serve_one_tcp_request: bind a synchronous socketserver.TCPServer to a given host/port, accept and process exactly one request with a caller-supplied echo/transform handler, then close the server and return the received and sent payloads.

**APIs**
- socketserver.TCPServer
- socketserver.BaseRequestHandler
- socketserver.BaseServer.handle_request
- socketserver.BaseServer.server_close
- socketserver.BaseServer.server_address

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"},"port":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":65535},"max_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1048576},"transform":{"type":"string","enum":["echo","upper","lower"]},"timeout_seconds":{"type":"number","minimum":0.1,"maximum":300}},"required":["host","port","max_bytes","transform"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"bound_address":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["string","integer"]},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2},"client_address":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["string","integer"]},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2},"received_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"received_text":{"type":"string"},"sent_text":{"type":"string"},"timed_out":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["bound_address","client_address","received_bytes","received_text","sent_text","timed_out"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Binds a listening TCP socket on the host for the duration of one request, accepts one client connection, reads up to max_bytes, writes a transformed response, then closes the socket and server. No persistent state, no files written, no background threads or processes.

**Constraints** Not available on WASI/WebAssembly platforms. Synchronous single-request only; no ThreadingMixIn or ForkingMixIn. Forking variants are POSIX-only and are not used here. IPv4/IPv6 depends on address_family; Unix domain sockets not exposed. Requires network binding permission on the worker; loopback-only recommended. This is a design proposal; no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- OSError (EADDRINUSE) when the requested host/port is already bound
- OSError (EACCES) when binding a privileged port without permission
- socket.gaierror when host cannot be resolved
- TimeoutError / handle_timeout path when no request arrives within timeout_seconds
- UnicodeDecodeError when received bytes are not valid UTF-8
- Payload exceeding max_bytes is truncated and flagged via received_bytes
- ValueError for invalid port or transform value
- Exception raised inside the handler triggers BaseServer.handle_error and is surfaced as an error result

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders validating a request/response handler pipeline against a real socketserver.TCPServer without writing a full server loop
2. Smoke-testing network egress/ingress and port binding permissions on a worker environment
3. Teaching and demonstrating BaseRequestHandler.handle() semantics with bounded, deterministic single-request execution
4. Generating reproducible fixtures of client/server byte exchanges for protocol parser tests
5. Prototyping echo/transform services that later graduate to serve_forever() with ThreadingMixIn

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html#module-sqlite3)

Execute a single parameterized SQL statement against a SQLite database connection and return the fetched rows, using sqlite3.connect() to open the connection and Cursor.execute()/fetchall() to run and retrieve results.

**APIs**
- sqlite3.connect(database, *, timeout=5.0, detect_types=0, isolation_level='DEFERRED', check_same_thread=True, factory=Connection, cached_statements=128, uri=False, autocommit=LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL)
- Connection.cursor(factory=Cursor)
- Cursor.execute(sql, parameters=(), /)
- Cursor.fetchall()
- Connection.commit()
- Connection.close()

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"database":{"type":"string","description":"Path to the SQLite database file, or \u0027:memory:\u0027 for an in-memory database."},"sql":{"type":"string","description":"A single SQL statement using qmark or named placeholders."},"parameters":{"type":["array","object"],"description":"Sequence for unnamed placeholders or object for named placeholders.","items":{}},"timeout":{"type":"number","description":"Seconds to wait on a locked table before raising OperationalError."},"readOnly":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, do not commit; intended for SELECT-only statements."}},"required":["database","sql"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"rows":{"type":"array","description":"Fetched result rows, each row a JSON array of column values.","items":{"type":"array","items":{}}},"rowCount":{"type":"integer","description":"Number of rows returned."},"committed":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether a commit was performed."}},"required":["rows","rowCount","committed"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Opens a file or in-memory SQLite database, may create the database file if absent, may implicitly open a transaction for DML statements, and may write changes to disk when committed. No network access; no external server process.

**Constraints** sqlite3 is an optional CPython module requiring the third-party SQLite library; availability depends on the Python build/distributor. All connect() parameters except database are keyword-only as of Python 3.15. check_same_thread defaults to True, restricting cross-thread use. Loadable extension support is not built by default. autocommit defaults to LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL and is slated to change. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- OperationalError when the database file cannot be opened or a table remains locked beyond timeout
- OperationalError when the SQL references missing tables or columns
- ProgrammingError when sql contains more than one statement
- ProgrammingError when named placeholders are used with a sequence of parameters
- IntegrityError when a constraint (e.g. UNIQUE, NOT NULL) is violated
- DatabaseError for malformed SQL or invalid serialized data
- InterfaceError when the connection or cursor is already closed
- OverflowError if bound integer values exceed SQLite's 64-bit range

**Ranked use cases**
1. Run a bounded parameterized SELECT/INSERT against a local SQLite file to persist structured records for a capability builder
2. Prototype data storage for an application before porting to a server database such as PostgreSQL
3. Query an in-memory ':memory:' database to validate SQL logic without touching disk
4. Use placeholders to safely bind untrusted values and avoid SQL injection in generated queries
5. Inspect sqlite_master to verify schema creation during setup or migration steps

- socket.timeout / TimeoutError when the connection or handshake exceeds timeout_seconds
- socket.gaierror for unresolvable host names
- ConnectionRefusedError / OSError for unreachable or refused endpoints
- ValueError from getpeercert() if the handshake has not completed
- ssl.SSLEOFError or ssl.SSLZeroReturnError if the peer closes abruptly or cleanly mid-handshake
- FileNotFoundError or ssl.SSLError when cafile/capath/cadata cannot be loaded

**Ranked use cases**
1. Pre-flight TLS posture audit of internal service endpoints before deploying capability workers that must reach them
2. Certificate expiry and chain-completeness monitoring for services consumed by automation pipelines
3. Verifying that a custom CA bundle (cafile/capath/cadata) correctly validates a target host before wiring it into a client context
4. Recording negotiated protocol version and cipher for compliance evidence and downgrade detection
5. Diagnosing hostname/SAN mismatches by comparing subjectAltName entries against the requested server_hostname

**Effects** Pure computation only; no filesystem access, no syscalls, no mutation. Deterministic and side-effect free.

**Constraints** Requires a caller-supplied st_mode integer; does not itself call os.stat/os.fstat/os.lstat. Results for door/port/whiteout types are platform-dependent (constants are 0 where unsupported). Windows-specific st_file_attributes and st_reparse_tag constants are out of scope for this operation. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- mode is not an integer or is negative -> validation error before calling stat functions
- mode is an integer but does not correspond to any known S_IF* type -> fileType 'other' with typeBits reported
- platform-specific types (door, port, whiteout) are defined as 0 on unsupported platforms, so they cannot be distinguished and fall through to 'other'
- stat.filemode may raise if given a value outside expected range on some implementations -> propagate as error

**Ranked use cases**
1. Classify a cached st_mode without re-invoking os.stat, avoiding repeated syscalls when testing many files (as in the documented walktree example)
2. Render human-readable permission strings ('-rwxrwxrwx') for file-listing or audit tooling
3. Detect special file types (block/char devices, FIFOs, sockets) that os.path.is* helpers do not cover
4. Build portable file-type filters for directory traversal pipelines
5. Extract permission bits for comparison against os.chmod masks in permission-management utilities

## string

Text Processing Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/string.html#module-string)

Render a bounded, validated $-template substitution using string.Template.safe_substitute, returning the rendered text plus the identifiers that were resolved and the identifiers left unresolved, without raising on missing placeholders.

**APIs**
- string.Template
- string.Template.safe_substitute
- string.Template.get_identifiers
- string.Template.is_valid
- string.capwords

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"template":{"type":"string","description":"Template text using $-placeholders ($$, $name, ${name})."},"mapping":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"description":"Placeholder name to replacement string."},"capitalize_words":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, apply string.capwords to the rendered result."}},"required":["template","mapping"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"rendered":{"type":"string"},"resolved":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"unresolved":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"valid":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["rendered","resolved","unresolved","valid"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure in-memory string transformation; no filesystem, network, locale mutation, or global state changes. Does not call locale.setlocale, so 'n' formatting behavior is unaffected. No installation or execution is claimed.

**Constraints** Standard library only; no third-party dependencies. Behavior is locale-independent for the constants and Template class. safe_substitute never raises on missing placeholders or stray '$', so callers must inspect unresolved/valid. Output size should be bounded by the caller. Platform-neutral across CPython 3.x supporting get_identifiers/is_valid (3.11+).

**Failure modes**
- Input fails JSON Schema validation (missing template or mapping, non-string values).
- Template contains a malformed placeholder; safe_substitute leaves it intact rather than raising, so validity is reported via the valid field (is_valid returns false).
- Mapping values are non-string and cannot be coerced; rejected at schema validation.
- Rendered output exceeds a configured size bound; operation must reject rather than truncate silently.
- capitalize_words applied to non-ASCII text may produce locale-independent but unexpected casing per str.capitalize semantics.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Safe i18n message rendering where missing translations must degrade gracefully instead of raising KeyError.
2. Configuration/notification templating for pipeline tooling that must report which placeholders were unresolved.
3. Pre-flight validation of user-authored templates before committing them to a render step.
4. Batch generation of human-readable labels from structured records with deterministic, locale-independent output.
5. Auditing template coverage by diffing declared identifiers against supplied mapping keys.

render_template: convert a string.templatelib.Template into a single rendered string by applying each Interpolation's conversion (via string.templatelib.convert) and format_spec (via format()), interleaving the static strings, and returning the result plus a per-interpolation audit record.

**APIs**
- string.templatelib.Template (attributes strings, interpolations, values; iteration; __add__)
- string.templatelib.Interpolation (attributes value, expression, conversion, format_spec)

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"template":{"type":"object","description":"A Template instance (or structurally equivalent object exposing strings and interpolations)"},"strict":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, reject interpolations whose format_spec is not accepted by format(); if false, fall back to str(value)","default":true}},"required":["template"]}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"rendered":{"type":"string","description":"The fully rendered output string"},"parts":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["string","interpolation"]},"text":{"type":"string"},"expression":{"type":["string","null"]},"conversion":{"type":["string","null"]},"formatSpec":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["kind","text"]}},"interpolationCount":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["rendered","parts","interpolationCount"]}
```

**Constraints** Requires Python 3.14+ where string.templatelib exists (t-strings added in 3.14); not available on earlier interpreters. Template and Interpolation are immutable, so rendering must not attempt attribute assignment. Concatenation of Template with str is unsupported by the module, so the operation must not rely on it. No installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed; this is a design proposal only.

**Failure modes**

- ValueError when len(strings) != len(interpolations)+1 (malformed template)
- ValueError when an Interpolation.conversion is not one of None, 'a', 'r', 's'
- ValueError/TypeError from format() when strict=true and format_spec is invalid for the value type
- TypeError when a value does not support the requested conversion or formatting
- AttributeError when an interpolation lacks value/expression/conversion/format_spec

**Ranked use cases**
1. Safe HTML/SQL/log message rendering: render a t-string template with escaping or parameterization applied per interpolation, preserving expression text for audit.
2. Localization/i18n pipelines: extract static strings and interpolation metadata from templates for translation catalogs, then re-render with translated segments.
3. Structured logging and telemetry: emit rendered messages plus per-interpolation records (expression, conversion, format_spec) for traceability.
4. Template validation/linting tooling: render templates in strict mode to surface invalid format specs or conversions before deployment.
5. Code generation and documentation builders: render t-string templates into source or docs while retaining interpolation provenance for review.

## struct

Binary Data Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/struct.html#module-struct)

pack_values: compile a struct format string once via struct.Struct and pack a bounded list of Python values into a bytes object, returning the format, computed size, and hex-encoded payload for inspection.

**APIs**
- struct.Struct(format) — compiles the format string once and exposes .size and .format, avoiding repeated compilation for repeated packing
- Struct.pack(v1, v2, ...) — packs the supplied values according to the compiled format and returns a bytes object whose length equals .size
- struct.calcsize(format) — returns the byte size required by a format string, used to validate expected size before packing

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"format":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"struct format string, e.g. \u0027\u003C10sHHb\u0027"},"values":{"type":"array","description":"Positional values matching the format; ints, floats, bools, bytes, bytearray, or complex per format characters","items":{}},"expectedSize":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional expected byte size; if provided must equal calcsize(format)"}},"required":["format","values"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"format":{"type":"string"},"size":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"hex":{"type":"string","pattern":"^([0-9a-f]{2})*$"},"byteLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["format","size","hex","byteLength"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure computation: no filesystem, network, or global state mutation. Returns a new bytes-derived hex string; does not write into caller buffers (pack_into is intentionally excluded to keep the operation side-effect free).

**Constraints** Native-mode formats ('@' or no prefix) depend on the host platform's C compiler sizes and alignment, so output bytes may differ across architectures; standard-mode formats ('=', '<', '>', '!') are platform-independent. 'n', 'N', and 'P' are only valid in native mode. 'e' requires Python 3.6+, 'Zf'/'Zd' require 3.15+, and 'F'/'D' are soft-deprecated. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- struct.error raised for malformed format strings (bad format character, invalid repeat count, whitespace inside a count)
- struct.error raised when the number of values does not match the format
- struct.error raised when an integer value is outside the valid range for its format character (e.g. 'h' requires -32768 <= number <= 32767)
- struct.error raised when a value type is incompatible with its format character (e.g. non-bytes for 's'/'c', non-numeric for numeric codes)
- struct.error raised when 'n', 'N', or 'P' are used with a non-native byte-order prefix ('=', '<', '>', '!')
- Size mismatch error when expectedSize is supplied and differs from calcsize(format)
- Input validation error when format is empty or values is not an array

**Ranked use cases**
1. Packing fixed-layout binary records (e.g. '<10sHHb' student records) for file or network interchange with explicit byte order
2. Encoding network-order headers and protocol fields using '!' big-endian formats for wire-format messages
3. Serializing numeric arrays or sensor samples into compact binary blobs for storage or transport
4. Building and validating C-compatible struct layouts in native mode for interop with compiled extensions
5. Producing deterministic test fixtures of packed bytes for parser and decoder test suites
