split_url_components: parse a single URL string into its scheme, netloc, path, query and fragment components using urllib.parse.urlsplit, returning the components plus derived hostname and port, without performing any network access or validation beyond what urlsplit itself does.

**APIs**
- urllib.parse.urlsplit(urlstring, scheme=None, allow_fragments=True, *, missing_as_none=False) — splits a URL string into a 5-item SplitResult named tuple (scheme, netloc, path, query, fragment) and exposes derived username, password, hostname and port attributes; this is the core API the operation wraps.
- urllib.parse.SplitResult.geturl() — recombines the parsed components back into a URL string; used to report a normalized form of the input alongside the split components.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string","description":"URL string to split; may be relative or absolute."},"default_scheme":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Scheme to use only if the URL does not specify one."},"allow_fragments":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If false, fragment identifiers are not recognized and are parsed as part of path or query."},"missing_as_none":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, absent components are returned as null instead of empty strings."}},"required":["url"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"scheme":{"type":["string","null"]},"netloc":{"type":["string","null"]},"path":{"type":["string","null"]},"query":{"type":["string","null"]},"fragment":{"type":["string","null"]},"username":{"type":["string","null"]},"password":{"type":["string","null"]},"hostname":{"type":["string","null"]},"port":{"type":["integer","null"]},"normalized_url":{"type":"string"}},"required":["scheme","netloc","path","query","fragment","username","password","hostname","port","normalized_url"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure in-memory string parsing; no network access, no file I/O, no mutation of external state. Leading C0 control and space characters are stripped and \n, \r and \t are removed from the input before parsing, so the reported normalized_url may differ from the raw input.

**Constraints** Requires a CPython 3.x runtime providing urllib.parse; the missing_as_none parameter requires Python 3.15 or later, so on earlier runtimes it must be emulated or rejected. Behavior is not fully RFC 3986 or WHATWG compliant and is not a validator. The itms-services scheme handling may be removed on iOS and optionally on macOS builds. No installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- ValueError raised when the netloc contains unmatched square brackets.
- ValueError raised when reading the port attribute if an invalid or out-of-range port is specified.
- ValueError raised when netloc characters decompose under NFKC normalization into '/', '?', '#', '@' or ':'.
- TypeError raised if str and bytes/bytearray data are mixed in a single call.
- UnicodeDecodeError raised if non-ASCII byte values are passed in byte input.
- No validation is performed: malformed or ambiguous URLs may succeed and yield surprising components, so callers must verify scheme, hostname and path defensively.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Splitting user-supplied or configuration-supplied URLs into scheme, host, path and query for routing, logging or allowlist checks before any fetch.
2. Extracting hostname and port from a URL to build connection targets or to compare against a permitted-host set.
3. Separating query and fragment from a URL so the query can be handed to parse_qs and the fragment handled separately.
4. Normalizing a URL via geturl for deduplication or cache keys while preserving the original components.
5. Diagnosing malformed URLs by surfacing ValueError conditions such as bad ports or unmatched brackets in netloc.

Internet Protocols and Support

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.request.html#module-urllib.request)

**APIs**
- urllib.request.urlopen(url, data=None, timeout, *, context=None) — opens the URL and returns a context-manager response object exposing url, headers, and status
- urllib.request.Request(url, data=None, headers={}, method=None) — constructs the request abstraction used to set method and headers
- urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler — handler class governing redirect behavior within an opener chain
- urllib.request.build_opener([handler, ...]) — assembles an OpenerDirector chaining handlers for controlled request behavior

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute, properly encoded http or https URL"},"timeoutSeconds":{"type":"number","minimum":0.1,"maximum":120,"description":"Blocking timeout for connection and read"},"maxBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1048576,"description":"Maximum number of response body bytes to read"},"headers":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional request headers"},"method":{"type":"string","enum":["GET","HEAD"],"description":"HTTP method; defaults to GET"}},"required":["url","timeoutSeconds","maxBytes"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"integer","description":"HTTP status code"},"finalUrl":{"type":"string","description":"URL of the response after any redirects"},"headers":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"description":"Response headers as name/value strings"},"bodyPreview":{"type":"string","description":"Decoded (utf-8, errors=replace) prefix of the body"},"bytesRead":{"type":"integer","description":"Number of body bytes actually read"},"truncated":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if body exceeded maxBytes"}},"required":["status","finalUrl","headers","bodyPreview","bytesRead","truncated"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Performs outbound network I/O to the target host (or configured proxy) and reads a bounded amount of response data; emits the urllib.Request auditing event with fullurl, data, headers, and method; may consult proxy environment variables and system proxy settings; no filesystem writes and no persistent state beyond any installed global opener.

**Constraints** Availability: not WASI (does not work on WebAssembly). On macOS, unsafe in programs using os.fork() because getproxies() uses a higher-level system API; set no_proxy='*' to avoid. Uses HTTP/1.1 and sends Connection: close. Timeout applies only to HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP connections. HTTPS requires ssl module support; custom SSLContext should set ALPN protocols. HTTP_PROXY is ignored when REQUEST_METHOD is set (CGI). Redirects to non-HTTP/HTTPS/FTP URLs raise HTTPError as a security measure. Data objects that cannot be re-delivered may fail on redirect or auth retry; no 100-continue support.

**Failure modes**
- URLError raised on protocol errors (e.g., connection refused, DNS failure, unsupported scheme)
- ValueError raised if url is not a valid URL
- TimeoutError (OSError subclass) if the server does not respond within timeoutSeconds
- http.client.RemoteDisconnected if the server closes the connection without a response
- http.client.BadStatusLine and other http.client.HTTPException subclasses propagate unchanged (not wrapped in URLError)
- HTTPError raised for non-2xx responses when default error handling is in effect
- ValueError from DataHandler on malformed base64 data URLs with missing padding
- URLError from FileHandler when a remote hostname is given for a file URL
- URLError from url2pathname when authority cannot be resolved on non-Windows platforms

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders probing endpoint reachability and status codes with strict timeouts and byte caps for safe health checks
2. Fetching small API or metadata documents (JSON/HTML head) for content extraction pipelines with bounded memory use
3. Validating redirect chains and final URLs for link-integrity auditing without unbounded following
4. Retrieving headers only (HEAD) to inspect content type, length, and caching directives before deciding to download
5. Testing proxy and authentication handler configurations in a controlled opener chain for network diagnostics

Caller must obtain robots.txt content by other means; this operation does not fetch it. Behavior follows RFC 9309 as implemented by the module. No claim of installation, availability on any worker, or execution is made.

**Failure modes**
- Invalid or malformed robots.txt lines are tolerated by the parser; unrecognized directives are ignored rather than raising
- crawl_delay returns None when the parameter is absent, inapplicable to the user agent, or syntactically invalid
- request_rate returns None when the parameter is absent, inapplicable, or syntactically invalid
- site_maps returns None when no Sitemap entry exists or entries are invalid
- can_fetch may raise on a malformed URL argument
- No network errors occur because read() is not used; callers must supply the document text themselves

**Ranked use cases**
1. Pre-flight crawl permission check for a URL before a spider fetches it, using a robots.txt document already retrieved
2. Rate-limit planning: extract crawl_delay and request_rate for a user agent to schedule polite request pacing
3. Sitemap discovery: extract Sitemap entries from a robots.txt document for downstream indexing pipelines
4. Compliance auditing: batch-evaluate a set of URLs against a stored robots.txt to flag disallowed paths
5. Test harness for robots.txt rule evaluation without network dependency, using fixture documents

- site.getusersitepackages()

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"moduleName":{"type":"string","const":"usercustomize"},"includeSearchPath":{"type":"boolean","default":false}},"required":["moduleName"],"additionalProperties":false}

- uuid.uuid5(namespace, name) — generates a deterministic SHA-1-based UUID from a namespace UUID and a name; used when version 5 is requested.
- uuid.UUID — immutable UUID object exposing .hex, .urn, .int, .version, .variant, .is_safe; used to normalize and report the generated value.

```json

Required when version is 3 or 5."},"name":{"type":"string","description":"Name to hash. Required when version is 3 or 5."},"node":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional 48-bit node for versions 1 and 6."},"clock_seq":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional 14-bit clock sequence for versions 1 and 6."}},"required":["version"],"additionalProperties":false}

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"uuid":{"type":"string","description":"Canonical 8-4-4-4-12 lowercase hex form."},"hex":{"type":"string","description":"32-character lowercase hex string."},"urn":{"type":"string","description":"URN form \u0027urn:uuid:...\u0027."},"int":{"type":"integer","description":"128-bit integer value."},"version":{"type":"integer","description":"UUID version number."},"variant":{"type":"string","description":"Variant name (e.g. \u0027RFC_4122\u0027)."},"is_safe":{"type":"string","enum":["safe","unsafe","unknown"],"description":"SafeUUID status."}},"required":["uuid","hex","urn","int","version","variant","is_safe"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure in-process computation; no filesystem, network, or persistent state is modified. uuid1()/uuid6() may invoke a separate program to obtain the hardware address on first call, which can be slow. No installation or execution is claimed.

**Constraints** Requires Python 3.14+ for versions 6, 7, 8 and for NIL/MAX; versions 1,3,4,5 available on all supported CPython 3.x. uuid1() may embed the host MAC address and thus leak privacy. uuid8() is not CSPRNG-backed by default; use uuid4() for security-sensitive identifiers. uuid3() uses MD5 and is not collision-resistant.

**Failure modes**

- ValueError when namespace string is not a valid UUID and not a recognized '@dns'/'@url'/'@oid'/'@x500' shorthand.
- ValueError when version is not one of 1,3,4,5,6,7,8.
- TypeError when name is not a string or bytes.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Deterministic idempotency keys: derive stable UUIDs from (namespace, name) via uuid5() so retried operations map to the same identifier.
2. Database-friendly primary keys: generate time-ordered UUIDv7 (or v6) values to improve index locality in storage systems.
3. Correlation and trace identifiers: mint random uuid4() values for request/span IDs in logging pipelines.
4. Content-addressed references: use uuid3()/uuid5() to fingerprint named resources (URLs, DNS names, OIDs) for deduplication.
5. Test fixtures and data seeding: produce reproducible UUIDs from fixed namespaces for deterministic test data.

{"type":"object","properties":{"env_dir":{"type":"string","description":"Target directory for the virtual environment (absolute or relative to cwd)."},"system_site_packages":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"clear":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"symlinks":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"upgrade":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"with_pip":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"prompt":{"type":["string","null"],"default":null},"upgrade_deps":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"scm_ignore_files":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"default":[]}},"required":["env_dir"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"env_dir":{"type":"string"},"env_name":{"type":"string"},"prompt":{"type":"string"},"executable":{"type":"string"},"env_exe":{"type":"string"},"env_exec_cmd":{"type":"string"},"bin_path":{"type":"string"},"bin_name":{"type":"string"},"lib_path":{"type":"string"},"platlib_path":{"type":"string"},"inc_path":{"type":"string"},"pyvenv_cfg_path":{"type":"string"},"include_system_site_packages":{"type":"boolean"},"pip_bootstrapped":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["env_dir","env_name","executable","env_exe","bin_path","lib_path","pyvenv_cfg_path","include_system_site_packages","pip_bootstrapped"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Creates the target directory and parent directories as needed; writes pyvenv.cfg with home and include-system-site-packages keys; creates bin (POSIX) or Scripts (Windows) with a copy or symlink of the Python executable; creates lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages (or Lib\site-packages on Windows); installs activation scripts; optionally bootstraps pip via ensurepip; optionally writes a .gitignore; with clear=true deletes existing contents of env_dir before creation. No activation occurs and no third-party packages are installed beyond pip bootstrapping.

**Constraints** Availability: not Android, not iOS, not WASI. Platform-specific layout (bin vs Scripts, symlink vs copy defaults). Environments are non-portable and non-movable; shebang lines embed absolute interpreter paths. On Windows, symlinks are supported but not recommended and PowerShell activation may require execution policy changes. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- PermissionError when the target directory or its parents cannot be created or written
- OSError/FileExistsError when env_dir exists and neither clear nor upgrade is set (per documented behavior for pre-3.4 semantics; modern behavior re-uses existing directory, so callers must not assume failure)
- ValueError when incompatible options are combined (e.g. upgrade with clear, as shown in the documented example)
- RuntimeError or subprocess failure from ensurepip when with_pip is true and pip bootstrapping fails
- Failure when symlinks=true but the platform/filesystem does not permit symlink creation
- Failure when upgrade_deps=true and PyPI is unreachable or pip upgrade fails
- Failure when scm_ignore_files contains an SCM name with no create_{scm}_ignore_file method
- ModuleNotFoundError/ImportError if venv is unavailable on the running platform (Android, iOS, WASI)
- Invalid env_dir (empty string, non-string) rejected by argument validation

**Ranked use cases**
1. Provision a disposable per-project isolated environment directory before running a build or test harness, returning the interpreter path for direct invocation without activation.
2. Create a clean environment with with_pip=true to serve as a reproducible base for later dependency installation from a requirements file.
3. Generate an environment with system_site_packages=true for tooling that must see OS-installed libraries while isolating project packages.
4. Recreate or upgrade an existing environment in place (upgrade=true) after the base Python interpreter has been upgraded, preserving the directory location.
5. Create an environment with scm_ignore_files=["git"] so the environment directory is automatically excluded from version control in a project checkout.

## warnings

Python Runtime Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#module-warnings)

capture_warnings: run a bounded callable under a temporary warnings filter and return the recorded warning records, restoring prior filter and showwarning state on exit

**APIs**
- warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)
- warnings.simplefilter
- warnings.filterwarnings
- warnings.formatwarning
- warnings.showwarning

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"action":{"type":"string","enum":["default","error","ignore","always","all","module","once"],"description":"Filter action applied inside the context"},"category":{"type":"string","description":"Warning category class name, e.g. DeprecationWarning; must be a Warning subclass"},"message":{"type":"string","description":"Regex matched against start of warning message"},"module":{"type":"string","description":"Regex matched against start of fully qualified module name"},"lineno":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":0},"append":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"format":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If true, include formatwarning() text per record"}},"required":["action"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"records":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"message":{"type":"string"},"category":{"type":"string"},"filename":{"type":"string"},"lineno":{"type":"integer"},"module":{"type":["string","null"]},"line":{"type":["string","null"]},"formatted":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["message","category","filename","lineno"]}},"count":{"type":"integer"},"restored":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["records","count","restored"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Mutates process-global warnings filter and showwarning() (or a ContextVar when context_aware_warnings is true) for the duration of the call; suppresses stderr output while recording; restores prior filter and showwarning on exit. No filesystem or network effects.

**Constraints** Bounded to a single callable invocation; not reentrant-safe across threads unless sys.flags.context_aware_warnings is true (default true only on free-threaded builds). Behavior of recorded objects' type is unspecified; only listed attributes guaranteed. SyntaxWarning may not be suppressible by runtime filters. No installation, availability or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- Invalid action string rejected by filterwarnings/simplefilter (ValueError)
- category not a Warning subclass (TypeError/AssertionError)
- Invalid regular expression in message or module (re.error)
- action 'error' causes matching warnings to raise the warning category as an exception, aborting the operation
- Callable raises its own exception; filter state must still be restored
- Concurrent use of catch_warnings when sys.flags.context_aware_warnings is false yields undefined behavior across threads

**Ranked use cases**
1. Test harness asserting that deprecated APIs emit DeprecationWarning with expected message and category
2. Library compatibility gate that surfaces ignored-by-default warnings (DeprecationWarning, ResourceWarning) during CI runs
3. Interactive shell or notebook that makes DeprecationWarning visible for user namespaces other than __main__
4. Application entry point that hides Python-level warnings from end users unless sys.warnoptions is set
5. Diagnostic tool converting selected warnings to errors to catch future breaking API changes early

## wave

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/wave.html#module-wave)

inspect_wav_header: open a WAV source in read-only mode via wave.open and return its declared stream parameters (channels, sample width, frame rate, frame count, format code, compression type) without decoding audio frames.

**APIs**
- wave.open(file, mode='rb')
- Wave_read.getparams()
- Wave_read.getformat()
- Wave_read.getcomptype()
- Wave_read.close()
- wave.Error

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","description":"Filesystem path to a WAV file to inspect read-only."},"maxFramesReported":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional cap on reported nframes; informational only, does not truncate the file."}},"required":["path"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"nchannels":{"type":"integer","minimum":1},"sampwidth":{"type":"integer","minimum":1},"framerate":{"type":"integer","minimum":1},"nframes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"format":{"type":"string","enum":["WAVE_FORMAT_PCM","WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT","WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE"]},"comptype":{"type":"string"},"compname":{"type":"string"}},"required":["nchannels","sampwidth","framerate","nframes","format","comptype","compname"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only: opens the file for reading, reads header metadata, and closes the stream via Wave_read.close(). No bytes are written, no file is modified, and no audio frames are decoded or returned. The caller-supplied path is not closed by the module if a file-like object were passed, but this operation passes a path so wave owns and closes the handle.

**Constraints** Requires a local filesystem path accessible to the process; no network or remote URL support. Only uncompressed PCM, IEEE float (3.15+), and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE with KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_PCM (3.12+) are supported. Read-only mode only; wave does not support read/write WAV files. Behavior of getformat() depends on Python version (3.15+). This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- wave.Error raised for files violating the WAV specification or hitting implementation deficiencies
- FileNotFoundError / PermissionError / OSError when the path is missing or unreadable
- Unsupported compression type (comptype other than 'NONE') surfaces as wave.Error
- Unsupported format code or invalid IEEE-float sample width (not 4 or 8 bytes) surfaces as wave.Error
- Malformed or truncated header causes wave.Error during open or getparams
- Non-WAV input (e.g., other container formats) raises wave.Error

**Ranked use cases**
1. Pre-flight validation of uploaded or generated WAV assets before downstream audio processing pipelines
2. Metadata extraction for cataloging and indexing audio corpora (channels, rate, duration from nframes/framerate)
3. Format gating to reject non-PCM or unsupported IEEE-float widths before invoking decoders
4. Duration and size estimation for streaming or chunked playback planning without reading frame data
5. Regression checks in test harnesses that assert WAV writer output headers match expected parameters

## weakref

Data Types

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/weakref.html#module-weakref)

weakref.probe_referent: given a live weak reference handle registered in a bounded in-process registry, report whether its referent is still alive and, if so, return a stable opaque token for it, without ever resurrecting or strongly retaining the referent.

**APIs**
- weakref.ref(object[, callback]) — creates the weak reference whose liveness is probed; calling it returns the referent or None
- weakref.getweakrefcount(object) — reports how many weak references/proxies currently target the referent, used as a diagnostic field
- weakref.getweakrefs(object) — enumerates existing weak reference and proxy objects for the referent, used to detect duplicate registration
- weakref.finalize(obj, func, *args, **kwargs) — registers cleanup tied to referent collection so registry entries are pruned deterministically
- weakref.WeakValueDictionary — backs the handle registry so entries vanish automatically when referents are collected

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"handle":{"type":"string","description":"Opaque handle previously issued by this operation for a registered weak reference"},"includeWeakrefCount":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, include getweakrefcount of the live referent in the result"}},"required":["handle"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"handle":{"type":"string"},"alive":{"type":"boolean"},"referentToken":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Opaque token identifying the live referent; null when not alive"},"weakrefCount":{"type":["integer","null"],"minimum":0,"description":"Present only when includeWeakrefCount was true and referent is alive"},"callbackPresent":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether the underlying weakref has a non-None __callback__"}},"required":["handle","alive","referentToken","callbackPresent"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only with respect to the referent: the operation never creates strong references, never resurrects collected objects, and never mutates the referent. It may cause registry pruning (removal of dead entries) and, if includeWeakrefCount is requested, invokes getweakrefcount which is side-effect free. No files, network, or subprocess effects.

**Constraints** CPython-specific behavior for some types (tuple and int are not weak-referenceable even when subclassed). Weak reference support requires '__weakref__' in __slots__ when slots are defined. Weak references are hashable only if the referent is hashable and only before deletion. Proxies are never hashable. Finalizers are not invoked during the late interpreter-shutdown window when module globals may be None, and finalizers created in daemonic threads may not run at exit. Callbacks run from most-recently-registered to oldest. Operation must be implemented with the ref() is not None idiom to remain thread-safe. No installation, availability, or execution is claimed by this proposal.

**Failure modes**
- UnknownHandle: handle not present in registry (never issued or already pruned)
- InvalidHandleType: handle is not a string
- ReferentNotWeakReferenceable: registration-time TypeError because the object type does not support weak references (e.g. list, dict, int, tuple, or __slots__ without '__weakref__')
- CallbackErrorSuppressed: exceptions raised by weakref callbacks are written to stderr and cannot be propagated, so registry pruning errors are only observable out-of-band
- HashAfterDeath: calling hash() on a weak reference first time after referent deletion raises TypeError; operation must avoid hashing dead references
- ProxyReferenceError: if a proxy is used instead of ref, attribute access after collection raises ReferenceError; operation must use ref() is not None idiom
- RaceOnLiveness: separate liveness test then dereference is unsafe under threads; operation must dereference once and branch on the returned value

**Ranked use cases**
1. Cache liveness probe: verify whether a large cached object (e.g. image or array) is still alive before attempting reuse, enabling bounded caches that do not pin memory.
2. Registry hygiene for object-ID maps: implement the documented id-to-object pattern with WeakValueDictionary and expose a safe probe so callers can check staleness without resurrecting objects.
3. Finalizer lifecycle inspection: report whether a registered weakref.finalize cleanup is still pending (alive) versus already executed or detached, supporting deterministic resource teardown audits.
4. Duplicate-reference diagnostics: use getweakrefcount/getweakrefs to detect that a referent already carries many weak references or proxies, flagging potential leaks in long-lived registries.
5. Thread-safe observer bookkeeping: provide a single-dereference liveness check for observer/subscriber lists held weakly, avoiding the race between separate liveness tests and dereference in multithreaded code.

## webbrowser

Internet Protocols and Support

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/webbrowser.html#module-webbrowser)

Open a single URL in the user's default browser via webbrowser.open, returning whether a browser launch was reported successful, without waiting for or controlling the browser session.

**APIs**
- webbrowser.open(url, new=0, autoraise=True) — module-level convenience function that displays the URL using the default browser and returns True if a browser was successfully launched, False otherwise; raises the webbrowser.open auditing event with argument url.
- webbrowser.Error — exception raised when a browser control error occurs, surfaced as a structured failure.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string","description":"URL (or, on some platforms, filename) to display; passed verbatim to webbrowser.open."},"new":{"type":"integer","enum":[0,1,2],"default":0,"description":"0 = same window if possible, 1 = new window if possible, 2 = new tab if possible."},"autoraise":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Raise the browser window if possible."}},"required":["url"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"launched":{"type":"boolean","description":"Value returned by webbrowser.open: True if a browser was successfully launched, False otherwise."},"url":{"type":"string","description":"Echo of the requested URL."},"new":{"type":"integer","enum":[0,1,2],"description":"Echo of the requested new-window mode."}},"required":["launched","url","new"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Launches or hands off to an external browser process or OS handler; may spawn a child process, may block on Unix text-mode browsers, and emits the webbrowser.open auditing event with the URL. No network access is performed by the module itself.

**Constraints** Availability: not WASI, not Android. Behavior is platform-dependent: on non-Unix platforms or with a remote browser the controlling process does not wait; on Unix without a remote browser it launches and waits. BROWSER environment variable (os.pathsep-separated, %s substitution) influences browser selection and, since 3.14, can reorder platform defaults. On iOS, BROWSER, autoraise, browser preference and new tab/window arguments are ignored and ctypes is required. Opening filenames is neither supported nor portable. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- webbrowser.Error raised by the underlying browser controller; reported as a structured error rather than a boolean.
- webbrowser.open returns False when no browser could be launched; this is a non-exception failure and must be surfaced as launched=false.
- On iOS, calls to open() fail if the ctypes module is unavailable.
- On Unix with only text-mode browsers, the calling process blocks until the user exits the browser, so the call may not return promptly.
- Invalid or malformed URL strings are not validated by the module; behavior is delegated to the launched browser or OS handler.
- Auditing event webbrowser.open may be observed or blocked by audit hooks, causing the call to fail or be denied.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders exposing a single safe 'open documentation URL in the user's browser' action for interactive agent or assistant workflows.
2. Local developer tooling that surfaces generated reports or artifacts (e.g., HTML output) to the user's default browser after a build step.
3. Onboarding or help flows that open a project's documentation site in a new tab on explicit user request.
4. Test harnesses or demos that verify browser-launch wiring by checking the boolean return of webbrowser.open without asserting on browser internals.
5. Desktop notification or alert pipelines that deep-link the user to a relevant web console page from a local script.

- winreg.QueryValueEx
- winreg.CloseKey

## winsound

MS Windows Specific Services

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/winsound.html#module-winsound)

play_system_sound_alias: play a named Windows registry sound alias (e.g. 'SystemExit') synchronously or asynchronously via winsound.PlaySound, with optional suppression of the default fallback sound.

**APIs**
- winsound.PlaySound(sound, flags) — calls the underlying Win32 PlaySound() to play a filename, alias, memory WAV image, or None to stop; raises RuntimeError on system error.
- winsound.SND_ALIAS — flag indicating the sound argument is a registry sound association name.
- winsound.SND_ASYNC — flag to return immediately and play asynchronously.
- winsound.SND_NODEFAULT — flag to suppress the system default sound when the alias is not found.
- winsound.SND_NOSTOP — flag to avoid interrupting a currently playing sound.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"alias":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Registry sound association name, e.g. \u0027SystemExit\u0027, \u0027SystemAsterisk\u0027."},"async":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, add SND_ASYNC so the call returns immediately."},"noDefault":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, add SND_NODEFAULT to avoid playing the system default sound on miss."},"noStop":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, add SND_NOSTOP to avoid interrupting a playing sound."}},"required":["alias"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"played":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if PlaySound returned without raising."},"alias":{"type":"string","description":"Echo of the requested alias."},"flags":{"type":"integer","description":"Bitwise OR of the winsound SND_* constants actually passed."},"asynchronous":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether SND_ASYNC was applied."}},"required":["played","alias","flags","asynchronous"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** May produce audible sound on the host Windows machine; with async=true the call returns before playback finishes. No filesystem writes, no network access, no persistent state. Passing None to PlaySound (not exposed here) would stop playback; this operation does not stop sounds.

**Constraints** Windows-only module (Availability: Windows). Requires an audio device/sound driver; headless or service-session workers may fail or be silent. SND_LOOP requires SND_ASYNC and is incompatible with SND_MEMORY; SND_MEMORY cannot be combined with SND_ASYNC. SND_PURGE and SND_NOWAIT are documented as unsupported on modern Windows and are not used. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- RuntimeError raised by winsound.PlaySound when the system reports an error (e.g. alias not found and no default registered, or driver failure).
- ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError when winsound is unavailable (non-Windows platform).
- Invalid input rejected before calling the API: empty alias, non-boolean flag fields, unknown extra properties.
- SND_NOSTOP may cause the sound to be skipped silently if another sound is playing (no exception, but no audible playback).
- SND_ASYNC returns before playback completes, so later errors in playback are not observable to the caller.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders emitting a non-blocking notification sound (SND_ALIAS|SND_ASYNC) when a long-running task completes.
2. Deterministic audible alert on critical failure using 'SystemHand' with SND_NODEFAULT to avoid masking a missing alias.
3. Accessibility/SoundSentry-aware notification path (future extension using SND_SENTRY) for users relying on visual-to-audio cues.
4. Smoke-testing Windows audio plumbing in a capability harness by playing a known alias and asserting no RuntimeError.
5. User-configurable UI feedback layer that maps application events to registry sound aliases without bundling WAV assets.

{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string","description":"HTTP status line as emitted by the application, e.g. \u0027200 OK\u0027."},"headers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}},"bodyBase64":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded response body bytes."},"stderrText":{"type":"string","description":"Captured wsgi.errors output."}},"required":["status","headers","bodyBase64","stderrText"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure in-process execution: the handler writes only to the caller-supplied stdout/stderr buffers and mutates only its own copy of environ. No sockets are opened, no files are served, and sys.stdin/sys.stdout/sys.stderr/os.environ are not read or modified. The application itself may perform arbitrary side effects and must be treated as untrusted.

**Constraints** wsgiref is a reference implementation and is explicitly not recommended for production; it performs only basic security checks. BaseCGIHandler is intended for CGI-like gateway protocols and emits a Status: header rather than an HTTP status line, so output is not directly wire-ready for an origin server. The stdout object must accept full-chunk writes like io.BufferedIOBase. wsgi.run_once/multithread/multiprocess flags are set from constructor arguments. No installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed by this proposal.

**Failure modes**
- Application callable cannot be imported or is not callable (ImportError/AttributeError/TypeError).
- Application raises before start_response is called; handler invokes error_output and emits the default 500 error page.
- Application raises after headers are sent; response is truncated and traceback is written to wsgi.errors.
- start_response called with malformed status string or non-list headers (AssertionError under wsgiref.validate).
- Application returns a non-iterable or yields non-bytes chunks (TypeError).
- environ missing required CGI keys, causing KeyError during setup_environ.
- stdout write fails or returns short writes, violating the BufferedIOBase-style contract.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Conformance-testing a WSGI application against a synthetic CGI environment without starting a server.
2. Building a FastCGI/SCGI gateway adapter that reuses BaseCGIHandler for request dispatch.
3. Reproducing and debugging CGI deployment behavior (e.g. IISCGIHandler path duplication) in a sandbox.
4. Wrapping legacy CGI scripts as WSGI applications for migration to a modern server.
5. Generating deterministic golden-response fixtures for regression tests of middleware stacks.

- Headers.get_all

```json

**Effects** Runs the supplied application callable in-process exactly once with a synthetic request. May write validator warnings to sys.stderr via the warnings module. Does not open sockets, bind ports, or start any server. No filesystem or network side effects beyond those the application itself performs.

**Constraints** Requires CPython 3.11+ where wsgiref.types exists. wsgiref is a reference implementation and not recommended for production; only basic security checks apply. Single request only; no concurrency, no real HTTP transport. Application object must be passed in-process, not serialized. Platform-independent pure Python; no OS-specific constraints.

- AssertionError raised by wsgiref.validate.validator for nonconforming application or server behavior; captured into assertion_errors
- Application raises an unhandled exception during invocation; reported as a failure with traceback summary

1. Type-check and conformance-test a WSGI application callable against wsgiref.types.WSGIApplication and StartResponse protocols before deployment
2. Generate synthetic WSGIEnvironment fixtures for unit tests of middleware using setup_testing_defaults
3. Detect PEP 3333 violations in framework-generated applications via wsgiref.validate.validator

## wsgiref.util

Internet Protocols and Support

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/wsgiref.html#module-wsgiref.util)

Reconstruct the full request URI from a WSGI environ dictionary using wsgiref.util.request_uri, optionally excluding the query string, and return the reconstructed URI together with the scheme guessed by wsgiref.util.guess_scheme.

**APIs**
- wsgiref.util.request_uri(environ, include_query=True) — builds the full request URI per PEP 3333 URL Reconstruction from SCRIPT_NAME, PATH_INFO, SERVER_NAME, SERVER_PORT, wsgi.url_scheme and QUERY_STRING
- wsgiref.util.guess_scheme(environ) — inspects the HTTPS environ variable to return 'https' or 'http'

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"environ":{"type":"object","description":"WSGI-compliant environment dictionary (string keys to string values)","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},"include_query":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Whether to append QUERY_STRING to the reconstructed URI"}},"required":["environ"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"request_uri":{"type":"string","description":"Reconstructed request URI"},"scheme":{"type":"string","enum":["http","https"],"description":"Scheme guessed from the environ"},"include_query":{"type":"boolean","description":"Echo of the include_query input"}},"required":["request_uri","scheme","include_query"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure computation: reads the supplied environ dictionary and returns a new result object. The input environ is not mutated; no network, filesystem or process side effects occur.

**Constraints** Requires a PEP 3333-compliant environ supplied by the caller; the binding performs no I/O and does not start a server. wsgiref is documented as a reference implementation not recommended for production, so results are suitable for tooling and testing rather than hardened request handling. Behavior depends on the Python version providing wsgiref.util; no installation or availability on any worker is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- environ is not a mapping or contains non-string keys/values, causing a TypeError or KeyError during reconstruction
- Required PEP 3333 keys (e.g. SERVER_NAME, SERVER_PORT, wsgi.url_scheme, SCRIPT_NAME, PATH_INFO) are missing, raising KeyError
- include_query is not a boolean and is coerced or rejected by the binding
- Non-ASCII or non-Latin-1 values in environ violate PEP 3333 'bytes in unicode' expectations and produce a malformed URI
- Malformed SERVER_PORT or PATH_INFO values yield a syntactically invalid URI without an error

**Ranked use cases**
1. Reconstructing canonical request URIs inside WSGI middleware for logging, routing and redirect generation
2. Building absolute URLs for link generation and Location headers in framework adapters
3. Deriving the effective scheme (http/https) behind CGI/FastCGI gateways for security-sensitive cookie and redirect decisions
4. Generating test fixtures and assertions for WSGI application unit tests that inspect environ-derived URLs
5. Normalizing request identity for caching keys, audit trails and rate-limiting in capability-building tooling

{"type":"object","properties":{"application":{"type":"object","description":"WSGI application callable (not JSON-serializable; supplied as a host-side reference)"},"environ":{"type":"object","description":"WSGI environ mapping of string keys to string values","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},"captureWarnings":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"maxBodyBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":1048576}},"required":["application","environ"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Status string passed to start_response, or null if never called"},"headers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}},"bodyChunks":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Body chunks decoded as latin-1 for transport"},"bodyTruncated":{"type":"boolean"},"assertionErrors":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"warnings":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"conformant":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["status","headers","bodyChunks","bodyTruncated","assertionErrors","warnings","conformant"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only with respect to external state; invokes the supplied application callable in-process, which may itself perform arbitrary side effects. No installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

**Constraints** Reference implementation only; not recommended for production and performs only basic security checks. Absence of errors does not guarantee full PEP 3333 compliance. Behavior of raised AssertionErrors is server-dependent. Warnings go to sys.stderr unless captured. Application callable cannot be expressed in JSON and must be supplied by the host.

**Failure modes**
- AssertionError raised by the validator for nonconforming application or server behavior (captured into assertionErrors)
- Application raises an unhandled exception during invocation
- start_response called more than once or with malformed status/headers
- Returned iterable yields non-bytes items or is not iterable
- Body exceeds maxBodyBytes and is truncated
- environ missing required PEP 3333 keys
- Warnings emitted via the warnings module when captureWarnings is true

**Ranked use cases**
1. Conformance-testing newly written WSGI applications before deployment
2. Validating middleware wrappers that sit between server and application
3. Regression-checking framework-generated WSGI callables in CI
4. Diagnosing malformed status/header/body returns during development
5. Auditing third-party WSGI apps for PEP 3333 deviations

## xml

Structured Markup Processing Tools

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.html#module-xml)

Validate a candidate XML element/attribute name and text payload against XML 1.0 lexical rules using xml.is_valid_name and xml.is_valid_text, returning per-field validity without parsing or constructing any XML document.

**APIs**
- xml.is_valid_name(name)
- xml.is_valid_text(data)

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","description":"Candidate element or attribute name to validate"},"text":{"type":"string","description":"Candidate XML 1.0 character data to validate"}},"required":["name","text"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"nameValid":{"type":"boolean"},"textValid":{"type":"boolean"},"allValid":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["nameValid","textValid","allValid"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure computation; no XML parsing, no file or network access, no global state mutation. Returns booleans only.

**Constraints** Requires Python 3.15+ (xml.is_valid_name and xml.is_valid_text added in 3.15). Validation is lexical only and does not check namespace well-formedness, uniqueness, or document structure. No SAX/Expat parser is invoked, so Expat version does not affect results.

**Failure modes**
- TypeError if name or text is not a str (e.g., bytes or None)
- UnicodeEncodeError or ValueError if input contains lone surrogates that cannot be represented
- Missing required field in input object rejected by schema validation
- Non-string JSON values (numbers, objects) rejected before reaching the API

1. Pre-flight validation of user-supplied element/attribute names before building XML with xml.etree.ElementTree, preventing malformed output.
2. Sanitizing or rejecting text payloads destined for XML serialization to avoid illegal C0 control characters and U+FFFE/U+FFFF.
3. Input validation layer for XML-generating APIs that must guarantee well-formed names and character data without parsing.
4. Test-fixture and fuzzing harnesses that need a fast, dependency-free oracle for XML 1.0 lexical legality.
5. Guard in data-ingestion pipelines that classify incoming field names/text as XML-safe before routing to downstream XML consumers.

{"type":"object","properties":{"source":{"type":"string","description":"XML text when source_kind is \u0027string\u0027, or a filesystem path when source_kind is \u0027path\u0027"},"source_kind":{"type":"string","enum":["string","path"],"default":"string"},"tag_name":{"type":"string","description":"Element tagName to match on START_ELEMENT"},"expand":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, call expandNode on matched nodes before serializing"},"max_matches":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000,"default":100},"max_fragment_chars":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":1000000,"default":10000}},"required":["source","tag_name"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"matched_count":{"type":"integer"},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"fragments":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"tag_name":{"type":"string"},"attributes":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},"expanded":{"type":"boolean"},"xml":{"type":"string"},"xml_truncated":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["tag_name","attributes","expanded","xml","xml_truncated"],"additionalProperties":false}},"events_seen":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["matched_count","truncated","fragments","events_seen"],"additionalProperties":false}

**Effects** Read-only parsing of the supplied XML source; no files are written and no network access is performed by the binding itself. The underlying parser may read the file at the given path. No global state is modified; the DOMEventStream is created and discarded per call.

**Constraints** Pure-Python standard library module (xml.dom.pulldom) built on xml.sax; no third-party dependencies. External general entities are not processed by default since Python 3.7.1; callers needing them must supply a configured parser, which this bounded operation does not expose. parseString accepts only str; bytes must go through parse() with a binary file object. __getitem__ on DOMEventStream was removed in 3.11, so iteration must use getEvent/for-loop. Behavior is subject to the platform's Python version (3.7.1+ semantics assumed).

**Failure modes**
- XML parse error (malformed document) raised by the underlying SAX parser
- source_kind 'path' with unreadable or nonexistent file
- source_kind 'string' with non-str input (parseString requires str)
- tag_name empty or not a string
- max_matches or max_fragment_chars out of allowed range
- expandNode called on a node that is not an Element or is no longer valid in the stream
- external entity processing disabled by default (3.7.1+), so documents relying on general external entities may fail or omit content
- memory growth if expand is true on very large subtrees

**Ranked use cases**
1. Streaming extraction of selected elements (e.g. 'item') from large XML feeds without building a full DOM, for capability builders assembling data-ingestion tools
2. Bounded, memory-safe inspection of XML payloads where only matching fragments are expanded and serialized on demand
3. Building a lightweight XML event-filtering utility that reports matched element attributes and optional subtree XML for downstream processing
4. Security-conscious parsing of untrusted XML where default external-entity suppression is desirable and only explicit fragments are materialized
5. Prototyping pull-parser-based validators or linters that need per-element context without recursive tree traversal

**Effects** Pure in-memory parsing: no filesystem, network, or subprocess access; no external entity resolution; no persistent state. The xmlparser instance is single-use and discarded after the call. Handler callbacks are invoked synchronously during Parse. No installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

**Constraints** Requires CPython with the xml.parsers.expat module (backed by pyexpat; direct pyexpat use is deprecated). Expat supports only UTF-8, UTF-16, ISO-8859-1 and ASCII encodings. One parser instance parses exactly one document; create a new parser per call. Namespace processing requires a one-character namespace_separator. Untrusted input should be handled per the XML security guidance; external entity handlers are intentionally not implemented. Protection-tuning methods (SetBillionLaughsAttackProtection*, SetAllocTracker*, SetReparseDeferralEnabled) are version-dependent (3.13/3.15) and should be feature-detected with hasattr. - ExpatError XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY under resource exhaustion

**Ranked use cases**
1. Safe structural inspection of untrusted XML: parse a document with a bounded event budget and return element/attribute/text summaries plus precise ExpatError line/column diagnostics for validation pipelines.
2. Configuration and manifest extraction: pull element names, attributes and text from XML config/manifest files into a normalized event list for downstream processing.
3. XML well-formedness gate: run a fast non-validating parse to accept or reject documents before handing them to heavier validators or schema processors.
4. Namespace-aware inventory: enumerate namespace prefix/URI bindings and expanded element names to audit XML documents for namespace hygiene.
5. Streaming-style ingestion of chunked documents: drive Parse incrementally with isfinal control to summarize large XML payloads without building a full DOM.

## zipapp

Software Packaging and Distribution

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipapp.html#module-zipapp)

Build a bounded executable Python zip application archive from a source directory using zipapp.create_archive, optionally embedding a shebang interpreter and a generated __main__.py entry point, and report the resulting archive metadata without executing it.

**APIs**
- zipapp.create_archive(source, target=None, interpreter=None, main=None, filter=None, compressed=False) — creates the application archive from a directory, file, or file object, writing the shebang line and __main__.py as specified
- zipapp.get_interpreter(archive) — reads back the shebang interpreter from an existing archive for verification/diagnostics

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"source_dir":{"type":"string","description":"Path to a directory containing Python code to package"},"target_path":{"type":"string","description":"Output .pyz file path"},"interpreter":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Shebang interpreter command, e.g. \u0027/usr/bin/env python3\u0027; null for no shebang"},"main":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Entry point of form \u0027pkg.module:callable\u0027; null if source already contains __main__.py"},"compressed":{"type":"boolean","description":"Use deflate compression for archive members"},"include_globs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional glob patterns; only matching relative paths are included via the filter callback"}},"required":["source_dir","target_path","compressed"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"archive_path":{"type":"string"},"interpreter":{"type":["string","null"]},"main":{"type":["string","null"]},"compressed":{"type":"boolean"},"member_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"archive_size_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"has_main_py":{"type":"boolean"},"executable_bit_set":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["archive_path","interpreter","compressed","member_count","archive_size_bytes","has_main_py","executable_bit_set"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Writes a new .pyz file at target_path; on POSIX, sets the executable bit on the target when an interpreter is supplied. Does not execute the archive, does not import packaged code, and does not modify source_dir. Caller-supplied file objects (if used) remain caller-owned and are not closed.

**Constraints** Requires Python 3.5+ (filter/compressed parameters require 3.7+). C-extension dependencies cannot be loaded from inside a zip archive and must be shipped separately. Shebang portability depends on target OS and Python launcher behavior; no 'X.Y or later' interpreter syntax exists. Archive must contain __main__.py at the zip root. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- source_dir does not exist or is not a directory
- target_path parent directory missing or not writable
- main omitted while source_dir lacks __main__.py (archive would not be executable)
- main specified while source_dir already contains __main__.py
- main string not of form 'pkg.module:callable'
- target_path equals source when copying an existing archive
- filter callback raises or returns non-boolean
- OSError/IOError during archive write (disk full, permission denied)
- interpreter string contains newline or invalid shebang characters

**Ranked use cases**
1. Package a directory of pure-Python application code into a single distributable .pyz with an embedded interpreter shebang for POSIX execution
2. Generate a __main__.py entry point from a 'pkg.module:callable' spec so a source tree without one becomes a runnable archive
3. Produce compressed standalone archives bundling vendored dependencies installed via pip --target for single-file distribution
4. Inspect and rewrite the shebang interpreter of an existing archive by re-creating it with a new interpreter value
5. Apply include/exclude glob filtering to build minimal archives that omit C-extension packages which cannot run from a zip

## zipfile

Data Compression and Archiving

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile)

Inspect a ZIP archive's central directory and report a bounded, read-only member listing with per-member metadata (name, sizes, compression method, CRC, timestamp, directory flag) without extracting any member data.

**APIs**
- zipfile.ZipFile (opened in mode 'r'; provides infolist(), namelist(), getinfo(), testzip(), and close())
- zipfile.ZipInfo (attributes filename, file_size, compress_size, compress_type, CRC, date_time, and method is_dir())
- zipfile.is_zipfile (magic-number validity check before opening)
- zipfile.BadZipFile (raised for malformed archives)
- zipfile.LargeZipFile (raised when ZIP64 is required but disabled)

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"archive_path":{"type":"string","description":"Filesystem path to the ZIP archive to inspect."},"metadata_encoding":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional codec name used to decode member names and comments."},"max_members":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":100000,"description":"Upper bound on members returned; listing is truncated beyond this."},"include_crc_check":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, run testzip() to validate CRCs (reads all member data)."}},"required":["archive_path"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"is_valid_zip":{"type":"boolean"},"member_count":{"type":"integer"},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"first_bad_member":{"type":["string","null"]},"members":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"is_dir":{"type":"boolean"},"file_size":{"type":"integer"},"compress_size":{"type":"integer"},"compress_type":{"type":"integer"},"crc":{"type":"integer"},"date_time":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":6,"maxItems":6}},"required":["name","is_dir","file_size","compress_size","compress_type","crc","date_time"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"required":["is_valid_zip","member_count","truncated","first_bad_member","members"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only. Opens the archive for reading and closes it; no members are extracted and no files are written to disk. If include_crc_check is true, all member data is decompressed in memory for CRC verification, which consumes CPU and memory proportional to archive contents. No network access and no mutation of the source archive.

**Constraints** Requires a seekable file for modes 'r' and 'a'. Multipart ZIP files are not supported. Decryption of encrypted members is supported but slow (native Python). Writing encrypted archives is not supported. Optional compression modules (zlib, bz2, lzma, compression.zstd) must be present for corresponding methods. ZIP64 archives over 4 GiB are handled only when allowZip64 is enabled. Member name encoding is an instance-wide setting via metadata_encoding. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- FileNotFoundError when archive_path does not exist or is not readable.
- BadZipFile when the file is not a valid ZIP archive or its central directory is corrupt.
- LargeZipFile when the archive requires ZIP64 support that is not enabled.
- KeyError from getinfo() if a member name is requested that is not present.
- NotImplementedError when a member uses an unsupported compression method during CRC validation.
- RuntimeError when a required optional compression module (zlib, bz2, lzma, compression.zstd) is unavailable.
- ValueError when operating on a closed ZipFile handle.
- OSError for I/O errors, permission problems, or resource exhaustion while reading.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Pre-flight validation of uploaded or generated ZIP archives before any extraction, using is_zipfile and testzip to detect corruption early.
2. Building an inventory/manifest of archive contents (names, sizes, compression ratios, timestamps) for indexing, auditing, or deduplication pipelines.
3. Guarding against decompression bombs by inspecting declared file_size and member counts before deciding whether to extract.
4. Detecting path-traversal or absolute-path member names in untrusted archives prior to extraction.
5. Selective retrieval planning: choosing which members to read via ZipFile.open/read based on metadata without extracting the whole archive.

```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"archivepath":{"type":"string","description":"Path to a ZIP file, or a path within a ZIP file (e.g. \u0027foo/bar.zip/lib\u0027)."},"fullname":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted module name to probe, e.g. \u0027pkg.mod\u0027."},"includeSource":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, also attempt get_source and report presence/length.","default":false}},"required":["archivepath","fullname"],"additionalProperties":false}

**Output contract**

Only .py and .pyc entries are considered importable; dynamic modules are disallowed. ZIP64 supported since 3.13; Zstandard-compressed entries supported since 3.15; archives with comments supported since 3.8. find_loader/find_module were removed in 3.12, so find_spec must be used. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- ZipImportError raised by zipimporter constructor when archivepath is not a valid ZIP archive (surfaced as a structured error, not a crash).
- ZipImportError from is_package/get_filename/get_source when the module cannot be found in the archive.
- get_source returns None when the module exists but the archive contains no source (e.g. only .pyc).
- OSError from get_data when the requested pathname is absent.
- Dynamic modules (.pyd/.so) inside the archive are not importable via zipimport and will not be reported as found.
- Malformed or truncated ZIP entries, or unsupported compression, may raise errors during inspection.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Pre-flight validation that a plugin ZIP bundle exposes an expected top-level module or package before adding it to sys.path.
2. Inventorying which modules and packages a distributed ZIP archive provides, including subpath-prefixed layouts.
3. Detecting source-less (.pyc-only) archives to warn about slower import behavior.
4. Diagnosing import failures by distinguishing 'module absent' from 'invalid archive' via ZipImportError.
5. Auditing archive contents for disallowed dynamic modules (.pyd/.so) that zipimport cannot load.

## zlib

Data Compression and Archiving

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zlib.html#module-zlib)

zlib_compress_bytes: compress a single in-memory bytes payload with zlib.compress, returning the compressed bytes plus the Adler-32 checksum of the original input for integrity verification.

**APIs**
- zlib.compress(data, level=Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION, wbits=MAX_WBITS) — performs the one-shot deflate compression of the input bytes and returns a bytes object; this is the core operation.
- zlib.adler32(data, value=1) — computes the unsigned 32-bit Adler-32 checksum of the original uncompressed input, used as an integrity tag in the result.
- zlib.error — exception type raised on compression errors, mapped to a structured failure.

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded bytes to compress"},"level":{"type":"integer","minimum":-1,"maximum":9,"default":-1,"description":"Compression level; -1 default, 0 none, 1 best speed, 9 best compression"},"wbits":{"type":"integer","default":15,"description":"Window bits / header format; 9..15 zlib header, -9..-15 raw, 25..31 gzip"}},"required":["data"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"compressed":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded compressed bytes"},"inputLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"outputLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"adler32":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":4294967295,"description":"Unsigned 32-bit Adler-32 checksum of the original input"}},"required":["compressed","inputLength","outputLength","adler32"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Pure in-memory computation; no filesystem, network or global state changes. Returns a new bytes object and an integer checksum. No side effects beyond CPU and memory consumption.

**Constraints** Requires a CPython build with the optional zlib module present; zlib is optional and may be absent depending on the distributor. Behavior of wbits ranges and available constants (e.g. Z_RLE, Z_FIXED, Z_BLOCK) depends on the linked zlib version. Not cryptographically strong; checksums must not be used for authentication. Single-shot API only; streaming inputs are out of scope for this operation.

**Failure modes**
- zlib.error raised by zlib.compress on compression failure (e.g. invalid internal state) — surfaced as a structured error.
- Invalid level outside -1..9 or invalid wbits range — rejected before calling the API.
- Input not valid base64 or not decodable to bytes — rejected with a validation error.
- Memory exhaustion for very large inputs since the operation is one-shot and holds full input and output in memory.
- Module unavailable in the interpreter build (zlib is an optional module) — reported as an environment error, not a compression error.

**Ranked use cases**
1. Compress small-to-medium byte payloads (e.g. serialized records) before storage or transport, with an Adler-32 integrity tag for verification.
2. Produce zlib-format or gzip-format (via wbits 25..31) compressed blobs for interoperability with gzip-compatible consumers.
3. Generate deterministic compressed fixtures and checksums for testing compression pipelines.
4. Pre-compress configuration or asset blobs in build tooling to reduce artifact size.
5. Compute and attach checksums to compressed data so downstream decompression can validate integrity.

[Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo)

- zoneinfo.ZoneInfo.key — read-only attribute returning the lookup key used to construct the zone
- zoneinfo.ZoneInfoNotFoundError — KeyError subclass raised when the key is not found on the time zone path
- zoneinfo.available_timezones() — returns the set of valid canonical IANA keys available on the time zone path (used only for optional membership pre-check)
- datetime.datetime(..., tzinfo=ZoneInfo(key)) — attaches the zone to a naive local datetime to derive utcoffset() and tzname()

**Input contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"key":{"type":"string","description":"IANA zone key, relative normalized POSIX path form, e.g. America/Los_Angeles"},"local_datetime":{"type":"string","description":"Naive ISO 8601 local datetime, e.g. 2020-11-01T01:00:00"},"fold":{"type":"integer","enum":[0,1],"default":0}},"required":["key","local_datetime"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Output contract**
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"key":{"type":"string"},"utc_offset_seconds":{"type":"integer"},"tzname":{"type":["string","null"]},"fold":{"type":"integer"},"is_ambiguous":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["key","utc_offset_seconds","tzname","fold","is_ambiguous"],"additionalProperties":false}
```

**Effects** Read-only with respect to time zone data: constructs or retrieves a cached ZoneInfo instance, which may populate the ZoneInfo class cache and may open files on TZPATH. Does not call reset_tzpath() or clear_cache(), so TZPATH and cache state are not modified. No network access; no writes to disk.

**Constraints** Not available on WASI/WebAssembly. Requires system time zone data or the tzdata package; on Windows system data is typically absent so tzdata is required. TZPATH entries must be absolute paths. ZoneInfo objects created via from_file cannot be pickled and are out of scope here. Keys are primary keys, not user-facing labels (CLDR recommended for display). This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

**Failure modes**
- ValueError from ZoneInfo(key) when key is not a relative normalized POSIX path or contains up-level references
- ZoneInfoNotFoundError (KeyError subclass) when no matching file exists on TZPATH and tzdata is unavailable
- ValueError when local_datetime is not a valid naive ISO 8601 datetime
- TypeError when fold is not an integer 0 or 1
- InvalidTZPathWarning may be emitted at import/reset time if PYTHONTZPATH contains relative components; not raised by this operation itself

**Ranked use cases**
1. Capability builders validating that a requested IANA zone key resolves before scheduling or timestamping work
2. Normalizing event timestamps to a target zone by deriving UTC offset and tzname for a given local datetime
3. Detecting ambiguous local times around DST transitions via fold and offset comparison
4. Pre-flight checks that a worker environment has usable time zone data (system or tzdata) for a required key
5. Producing canonical zone identifiers for storage and interchange instead of user-facing display strings
